title.zh: 卷一百九十六上 列傳第一百四十六上: 吐蕃上
title.raw: 卷一百九十六上 列傳第一百四十六上: 吐蕃上 Volume 196 Biographies 146: Tubo (Tibet) 1

sentences.zh: 其國人號其王為贊普，相為大論、小論，以統理國事。

translations.literal: The people of the state called their king zanpu; they appointed one another as great lun and minor lun to govern state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The people addressed their sovereign as zanpu and set up great and minor councillors to administer the affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 無文字，刻木結繩為約。

translations.literal: They had no writing; they carved wood and tied knots to make agreements.
translations.idiomatic: They possessed no written script and relied on carved marks and knotted cords to record their agreements.

sentences.zh: 雖有官，不常厥職，臨時統領。

translations.literal: Although they had officials, they did not permanently hold their posts but took command on a temporary basis.
translations.idiomatic: Though offices existed, incumbents did not hold them permanently; leadership was assigned ad hoc as need arose.

sentences.zh: 征兵用金箭，寇至舉烽燧，百里一亭。

translations.literal: To levy troops they used golden arrows; when invaders came they raised beacon fires, with one relay station every hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: Conscription was signaled with golden arrows; at the approach of raiders beacon fires were lit, and relay stations stood every hundred li along the routes.

sentences.zh: 用刑嚴峻，小罪剜眼鼻，或皮鞭鞭之，但隨喜怒而無常科。

translations.literal: Punishments were severe: for minor offenses eyes and noses were gouged out, or offenders were flogged with leather whips, all according to the ruler's pleasure and anger without fixed statutes.
translations.idiomatic: Their penal code was harsh: even petty crimes might cost an eye or a nose, or bring a flogging with leather whips—yet punishment followed the ruler's mood rather than any fixed law.

sentences.zh: 囚人於地牢，深數丈，二三年方出之。

translations.literal: Prisoners were confined in underground dungeons several zhang deep and were not released until two or three years had passed.
translations.idiomatic: Captives were thrown into pits dug several zhang deep in the earth and might not see daylight again for two or three years.

sentences.zh: 宴異國賓客，必驅牦牛，令客自射牲以供饌。

translations.literal: When entertaining foreign guests, they always drove out yak and made the guests shoot the beast themselves to supply the feast.
translations.idiomatic: When they feasted guests from abroad, they would drive out a yak and require the visitors to shoot the animal themselves for the meal.

sentences.zh: 與其臣下一年一小盟，刑羊狗獼猴，先折其足而殺之，繼裂其腸而屠之。

translations.literal: With their ministers they held a minor covenant once a year, executing sheep, dogs, and monkeys—first breaking their legs to kill them, then splitting their bellies to butcher them.
translations.idiomatic: Once a year they swore a lesser oath with their ministers, sacrificing sheep, dogs, and monkeys by first breaking their legs, then gutting and dismembering them.

sentences.zh: 令巫者告於天地山川日月星辰之神云：「若心遷變，懷奸反覆，神明鑒之，同於羊狗。

translations.literal: They had shamans declare to the spirits of heaven and earth, mountains and rivers, sun, moon, and stars: "If your hearts change and you harbor treachery and turn back, the spirits will witness it, and you shall fare as these sheep and dogs."
translations.idiomatic: Shamans proclaimed to the spirits of heaven and earth, of mountains and rivers, sun, moon, and stars: "Should any heart turn traitorous or faithless, the gods will see it, and your fate shall be that of these sheep and dogs."

sentences.zh: 」三年一大盟，夜於壇墠之上與眾陳設肴饌，殺犬馬牛驢以為牲，咒曰：「爾等鹹須同心戮力，共保我家，惟天神地祇，共知爾誌。

translations.literal: " Every three years they held a great covenant. At night on the altar terrace they spread out food and drink for the multitude, slaughtering dogs, horses, cattle, and donkeys as victims, and chanted: "You must all unite your hearts and strength to guard our house together; only the spirits of heaven and earth shall know your intent."
translations.idiomatic: " Every three years came the great oath. At night upon the sacred terrace they laid out a feast for the assembly and sacrificed dogs, horses, cattle, and donkeys, intoning: "You must all join in single purpose to defend our house; heaven and earth alone shall witness your pledge."

sentences.zh: 有負此盟，使爾身體屠裂，同於此牲。」

translations.literal: Whoever breaks this covenant—may your bodies be torn apart like these victims."
translations.idiomatic: Whoever betrays this oath—may your bodies be hacked apart like these sacrificial beasts."

sentences.zh: 其地氣候大寒，不生秔稻，有青稞麥、褭豆、小麥、喬麥。

translations.literal: The climate of their land was bitterly cold; polished rice did not grow there, but they had highland barley, broad beans, wheat, and buckwheat.
translations.idiomatic: Their country was fiercely cold and could not grow rice; instead they cultivated highland barley, broad beans, wheat, and buckwheat.

sentences.zh: 畜多牦牛豬犬羊馬。

translations.literal: Their livestock were mostly yak, pigs, dogs, sheep, and horses.
translations.idiomatic: They raised chiefly yaks, pigs, dogs, sheep, and horses.

sentences.zh: 又有天鼠，狀如雀鼠，其大如貓，皮可為裘。

translations.literal: There were also "heaven mice," shaped like sparrow-mice but as large as cats; their pelts could be made into fur coats.
translations.idiomatic: They also had marmots—creatures like large rats, cat-sized—which furnished pelts for fur garments.

sentences.zh: 又多金銀銅錫。

translations.literal: Gold, silver, copper, and tin were also abundant.
translations.idiomatic: Gold, silver, copper, and tin were likewise plentiful.

sentences.zh: 其人或隨畜牧而不常厥居，然頗有城郭。

translations.literal: The people sometimes followed their herds in pastoral movement without fixed dwellings, yet they also had quite a few walled settlements.
translations.idiomatic: By custom many followed their herds and had no permanent home, yet they also maintained a fair number of walled towns.

sentences.zh: 其國都城號為邏些城。

translations.literal: The capital of their state was called Luoxie City.
translations.idiomatic: Their national capital was known as Luoxie City.

sentences.zh: 屋皆平頭，高者至數十尺。

translations.literal: All dwellings had flat roofs; the tallest rose to several tens of feet.
translations.idiomatic: Their houses were flat-roofed, some rising dozens of feet high.

sentences.zh: 貴人處於大氈帳，名為拂廬。

translations.literal: Nobles dwelt in great felt tents called fulu.
translations.idiomatic: Men of rank lived in large felt pavilions known as fulu.

sentences.zh: 寢處汙穢，絕不櫛沐。

translations.literal: Their sleeping quarters were filthy, and they never combed their hair or bathed.
translations.idiomatic: They slept amid filth and never combed their hair or washed their bodies.

sentences.zh: 接手飲酒，以氈為盤，撚鋋為碗，實以羹酪，並而食之。

translations.literal: They drank wine from cupped hands, used felt as platters, twisted iron into bowls, filled them with broth and curds, and ate everything together.
translations.idiomatic: They drank by cupping wine in their palms, served food on felt mats, shaped iron into bowls, heaped them with broth and curds, and ate all from the same dish.

sentences.zh: 多事羱羝之神，人信巫覡。

translations.literal: They devoted themselves chiefly to the god of the wild goat; the people trusted shamans.
translations.idiomatic: They worshipped chiefly the wild-goat deity, and the people placed their faith in shamans.

sentences.zh: 不知節候，麥熟為歲首。

translations.literal: They did not know the seasons and took the ripening of wheat as the year's beginning.
translations.idiomatic: Unacquainted with the calendrical seasons, they reckoned the ripening of wheat as the start of the year.

sentences.zh: 圍棋陸博，吹蠡鳴鼓為戲，弓劍不離身。

translations.literal: For amusement they played weiqi and liubo, blew horns and beat drums; bow and sword never left their persons.
translations.idiomatic: They passed the time with weiqi and liubo, with horn-blowing and drumming; bow and sword were never far from their side.

sentences.zh: 重壯賤老，母拜於子，子倨於父，出入皆少者在前，老者居其後。

translations.literal: They valued the strong and slighted the aged; mothers bowed to sons, sons were arrogant toward fathers; when going in and out, the young went ahead and the old behind.
translations.idiomatic: Youth and vigor were honored, age despised: mothers bowed to their sons, sons showed insolence toward their fathers; in procession the young led and the old followed behind.

sentences.zh: 軍令嚴肅，每戰，前隊皆死，後隊方進。

translations.literal: Military orders were stern: in every battle the front rank had to die before the rear rank advanced.
translations.idiomatic: Their military discipline was severe: in battle the front rank had to be cut down before the rear rank might advance.

sentences.zh: 重兵死，惡病終。

translations.literal: They prized death in battle and despised dying of illness.
translations.idiomatic: They honored death on the battlefield and scorned a death from sickness.

sentences.zh: 累代戰沒，以為甲門。

translations.literal: Families whose men had fallen in battle generation after generation were regarded as foremost houses.
translations.idiomatic: Clans that had lost men in war for generations were counted among the foremost families.

sentences.zh: 臨陣敗北者，懸狐尾於其首，表其似狐之怯，稠人廣眾，必以徇焉，其俗恥之，以為次死。

translations.literal: Those who fled in battle had fox tails hung from their heads to show their fox-like cowardice; before dense crowds they were always paraded in disgrace—a shame their custom ranked second only to death.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers who broke in battle had fox tails tied to their heads to mark their cravenness; they were then displayed before the multitude in ritual humiliation—a disgrace their people considered scarcely less than death itself.

sentences.zh: 拜必兩手據地，作狗吠之聲，以身再揖而止。

translations.literal: When bowing they always placed both hands on the ground, uttered a sound like a dog's bark, and stopped after bowing the body twice.
translations.idiomatic: To salute they pressed both palms to the earth, barked like dogs, and rose only after bowing their bodies twice.

sentences.zh: 居父母喪，截發，青黛塗面，衣服皆黑，既葬即吉。

translations.literal: In mourning for parents they cut their hair, painted their faces with indigo, wore only black clothing, and returned to normal life as soon as burial was done.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning parents they shaved their heads, stained their faces with indigo, dressed entirely in black, and resumed ordinary life the moment the burial was over.

sentences.zh: 其贊普死，以人殉葬，衣服珍玩及嘗所乘馬弓劍之類，皆悉埋之。

translations.literal: When a zanpu died, human victims were buried with him; garments, precious objects, and the horses, bows, and swords he had used were all interred.
translations.idiomatic: At a zanpu's death living retainers were sacrificed for burial, and his robes, treasures, and the horses, bows, and swords he had ridden and wielded were all laid in the tomb.

sentences.zh: 仍於墓上起大室，立土堆，插雜木為祠祭之所。

translations.literal: They also raised a great chamber over the tomb, piled an earthen mound, and planted miscellaneous trees as the place for sacrificial rites.
translations.idiomatic: Over the grave they built a great chamber and heaped an earthen mound, planting trees about it as the site for offerings.

sentences.zh: 貞觀八年，其贊普棄宗弄贊始遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Zhenguan, their zanpu Qizong Nongzan first sent envoys to offer tribute at court.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of the Zhenguan reign, the zanpu Qizong Nongzan—Songtsen Gampo—first dispatched envoys to present tribute at the Tang court.

sentences.zh: 弄贊弱冠嗣位，性驍武，多英略，其鄰國羊同及諸羌並賓伏之。

translations.literal: Nongzan succeeded while still in his youth; he was fierce and martial by nature and possessed many bold stratagems; the neighboring state of Yangtong and the various Qiang all submitted to him as guests.
translations.idiomatic: Nongzan had come to the throne barely out of boyhood. Bold and warlike, rich in stratagem, he brought the neighboring realm of Yangtong and the Qiang tribes under his sway.

sentences.zh: 太宗遣行人馮德遐往撫慰之。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong sent the itinerant envoy Feng Dexia to go and comfort him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong dispatched the itinerant envoy Feng Dexia to offer reassurance.

sentences.zh: 見德遐，大悅。

translations.literal: When he saw Dexia, he was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: On meeting Dexia he was delighted.

sentences.zh: 聞突厥及吐谷渾皆尚公主，乃遣使隨德遐入朝，多賫金寶，奉表求婚，太宗未之許。

translations.literal: Hearing that both the Turks and the Tuyuhun had been given imperial princesses in marriage, he sent envoys to follow Dexia to court with many gifts of gold and treasure, presenting a memorial to request a princess; Taizong did not grant it.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that the Turks and the Tuyuhun had each received Tang princesses, he sent envoys to accompany Dexia to court laden with gold and jewels, petitioning for a royal bride. Taizong refused.

sentences.zh: 使者既返，言於弄贊曰：「初至大國，待我甚厚，許嫁公主。

translations.literal: When the envoys returned, they said to Nongzan: "When we first arrived in the great state, we were treated very generously and were promised a princess in marriage."
translations.idiomatic: When the envoys returned they told Nongzan: "At first the Great State received us with great honor and promised us a princess."

sentences.zh: 會吐谷渾王入朝，有相離間，由是禮薄，遂不許嫁。

translations.literal: It happened that the king of Tuyuhun came to court; there was mutual slander between them, and for this reason our treatment grew cold, and the marriage was not granted."
translations.idiomatic: But then the Tuyuhun king arrived at court and slandered us; our reception grew cold, and the marriage was denied."

sentences.zh: 」弄贊遂與羊同連，發兵以擊吐谷渾。

translations.literal: Nongzan then joined with Yangtong and launched troops to attack Tuyuhun.
translations.idiomatic: Nongzan thereupon allied with Yangtong and marched against Tuyuhun.

sentences.zh: 吐谷渾不能支，遁於青海之上，以避其鋒。

translations.literal: Tuyuhun could not withstand them and fled to the shores of Qinghai to escape their edge.
translations.idiomatic: Tuyuhun could not hold its ground and withdrew to the Qinghai lakes to escape the Tibetan advance.

sentences.zh: 其國人畜並為吐蕃所掠。

translations.literal: The people and livestock of their state were all plundered by Tubo.
translations.idiomatic: The people and herds of Tuyuhun were carried off by the Tibetans.

sentences.zh: 於是進兵攻破党項及白蘭諸羌，率其眾二十余萬，頓於松州西境。

translations.literal: Thereupon he advanced and broke the Tangut and the various Qiang of Bailan, leading more than two hundred thousand of his followers to encamp on the western border of Songzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He then pushed forward, crushing the Tangut and the Bailan Qiang, and camped with more than two hundred thousand men on the western marches of Song Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 遣使貢金帛，雲來迎公主。

translations.literal: He sent envoys bearing gold and silks, saying they had come to welcome the princess.
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched envoys with gold and silks, declaring that they had come to escort the princess home.

sentences.zh: 又謂其屬曰：「若大國不嫁公主與我，即當入寇。

translations.literal: He also told his followers: "If the great state will not give me a princess in marriage, I shall invade at once."
translations.idiomatic: He told his chiefs as well: "If the Great State refuses me a princess, I shall raid its borders."

sentences.zh: 」遂進攻松州，都督韓威輕騎覘賊，反為所敗，邊人大擾。

translations.literal: He then advanced to attack Songzhou. Protector-general Han Wei took light cavalry to reconnoiter the enemy and was in turn defeated; the border people were greatly alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon attacked Song Prefecture. Protector-general Han Wei rode out with a light force to scout the enemy and was routed; the frontier populace was thrown into turmoil.

sentences.zh: 太宗遣吏部尚書侯君集為當彌道行營大總管，右領軍大將軍執失思力為白蘭道行軍總管，左武衛將軍牛進達為闊水道行軍總管，右領軍將軍劉蘭為洮河道行軍總管，率步騎五萬以擊之。

translations.literal: Taizong sent Minister of Personnel Hou Junji as grand commander of the Dangmi circuit campaign headquarters, Right Leader of the Palace Guards Zhishi Sili as marching commander of the Bailan route, Left Martial Guard general Niu Jinda as marching commander of the Kuoshui route, and Right Leader of the Palace Guards Liu Lan as marching commander of the Taohe route, leading fifty thousand infantry and cavalry to strike them.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong appointed Hou Junji, Minister of Personnel, grand commander of the Dangmi campaign; Zhishi Sili, Right Leader of the Palace Guards, commander on the Bailan route; Niu Jinda of the Left Martial Guard on the Kuoshui route; and Liu Lan of the Right Leader of the Palace Guards on the Taohe route—with fifty thousand foot and horse to drive the Tibetans back.

sentences.zh: 進達先鋒自松州夜襲其營，斬千余級。

translations.literal: Jinda's vanguard made a night raid on their camp from Songzhou and beheaded more than a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Niu Jinda's vanguard stole out of Song Prefecture by night, fell on the Tibetan camp, and took more than a thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 弄贊大懼，引兵而退，遣使謝罪。

translations.literal: Nongzan was greatly afraid, withdrew his army, and sent envoys to apologize.
translations.idiomatic: Nongzan was terrified, pulled his army back, and sent envoys to beg forgiveness.

sentences.zh: 因復請婚，太宗許之。

translations.literal: He then again requested marriage, and Taizong granted it.
translations.idiomatic: He renewed his suit for a princess, and Taizong consented.

sentences.zh: 弄贊乃遣其相祿東贊致禮，獻金五千兩，自余寶玩數百事。

translations.literal: Nongzan then sent his minister Gar Tongtsen to present gifts: five thousand liang of gold and several hundred other precious objects besides.
translations.idiomatic: Nongzan dispatched his minister Gar Tongtsen with betrothal gifts—five thousand liang of gold and several hundred other treasures besides.

sentences.zh: 貞觀十五年，太宗以文成公主妻之，令禮部尚書、江夏郡王道宗主婚，持節送公主於吐蕃。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Zhenguan, Taizong gave him Princess Wencheng in marriage, ordered Minister of Rites and Prince of Jiangxia Li Daozong to preside over the wedding, and sent him with credentials of office to escort the princess to Tubo.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year of Zhenguan, Taizong wed Princess Wencheng to him, appointing Li Daozong, Minister of Rites and Prince of Jiangxia, to oversee the marriage and escort the princess to Tubo with full diplomatic credentials.

sentences.zh: 弄贊率其部兵次柏海，親迎於河源。

translations.literal: Nongzan led his tribal troops to encamp at Bohai and went in person to welcome her at Heyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Nongzan marched his forces to Bohai and went in person to receive her at the headwaters of the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 見道宗，執子婿之禮甚恭。

translations.literal: When he met Daozong, he observed the courtesy of a son-in-law with great respect.
translations.idiomatic: On meeting Daozong he received him with the deference due a father-in-law.

sentences.zh: 既而嘆大國服飾禮儀之美，俯仰有愧沮之色。

translations.literal: Presently he sighed at the beauty of the great state's dress and ritual, and in his bearing showed shame and dejection.
translations.idiomatic: He soon marveled at the splendor of Tang dress and ceremony, and in his manner betrayed shame at his own people's rustic ways.

sentences.zh: 及與公主歸國，謂所親曰：「我父祖未有通婚上國者，今我得尚大唐公主，為幸實多。

translations.literal: When he returned home with the princess, he said to those close to him: "My fathers and grandfathers never married into the upper state; now that I have been given a princess of Great Tang, my good fortune is indeed great."
translations.idiomatic: Returning home with the princess, he told his intimates: "None of my forebears ever married into the Great State; that I have wed a princess of Tang is fortune beyond measure."

sentences.zh: 當為公主築一城，以誇示後代。

translations.literal: I ought to build a city for the princess, to display our glory to later generations."
translations.idiomatic: I shall build her a city, that posterity may see what honor she brought us."

sentences.zh: 」遂築城邑，立棟宇以居處焉。

translations.literal: He then built walled towns and erected timber halls for dwelling.
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon raised walled settlements and timber halls in which to live.

sentences.zh: 公主惡其人赭面，弄贊令國中權且罷之，自亦釋氈裘，襲紈綺，漸慕華風。

translations.literal: The princess disliked the people's custom of reddening their faces; Nongzan ordered the realm provisionally to abandon it. He himself also put aside felt robes, donned silk gauze, and gradually came to admire Chinese ways.
translations.idiomatic: The princess detested the Tibetan custom of painting the face red; Nongzan ordered the practice suspended throughout the realm. He himself laid aside felt garments for silks and slowly grew enamored of Tang civilization.

sentences.zh: 仍遣酋豪子弟，請入國學以習《詩》、《書》。

translations.literal: He also sent sons of tribal chiefs to request admission to the National University to study the Odes and Documents.
translations.idiomatic: He sent sons of the chieftains to petition for places in the National University to study the Odes and Documents.

sentences.zh: 又請中國識文之人典其表疏。

translations.literal: He further requested literate men from China to manage his memorials and correspondence.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked for Chinese literati to draft his state papers and memorials.

sentences.zh: 太宗伐遼東還，遣祿東贊來賀。

translations.literal: When Taizong returned from campaigning in Liaodong, he sent Gar Tongtsen to offer congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: On Taizong's return from the Liaodong campaign, Gar Tongtsen was dispatched to offer congratulations.

sentences.zh: 奉表曰：「聖天子平定四方，日月所照之國，並為臣妾，而高麗恃遠，闕於臣禮。

translations.literal: He presented a memorial saying: "The sage Son of Heaven has pacified the four quarters; every land touched by sun and moon has become his subject, yet Goryeo, relying on its distance, lacks the rites of a vassal."
translations.idiomatic: In his memorial he wrote: "The sage Son of Heaven has pacified the four quarters; every realm beneath sun and moon bows as his subject—yet Goryeo, trusting in its remoteness, neglects the duties of vassalage."

sentences.zh: 天子自領百萬，度遼致討，隳城陷陣，指日凱旋。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven himself led a million men, crossed the Liao to punish them, shattered their walls and broke their battle lines, and was to return in triumph within days."
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven led a million men in person across the Liao to chastise them, razed their walls and broke their ranks, and was to return in triumph within days."

sentences.zh: 夷狄才聞陛下發駕，少進之間，已聞歸國。

translations.literal: We barbarians had only just heard that Your Majesty had set out; after advancing but a little we already heard you had returned home.
translations.idiomatic: We barbarians had scarcely heard that Your Majesty had marched forth when, after barely setting out, we learned you were already home again.

sentences.zh: 雁飛迅越，不及陛下速疾。

translations.literal: Wild geese fly swiftly in flight, yet they cannot match Your Majesty's speed.
translations.idiomatic: Even wild geese in swift flight cannot keep pace with Your Majesty's haste.

sentences.zh: 奴忝預子婿，喜百常夷。

translations.literal: Your slave, who unworthily shares the status of son-in-law, is a hundred times happier than ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Your humble son-in-law rejoices beyond all measure.

sentences.zh: 夫鵝，猶雁也，故作金鵝奉獻。

translations.literal: Now the goose is like the wild goose; therefore I have made a golden goose to present as tribute."
translations.idiomatic: The goose is kin to the wild goose; I have therefore cast a golden goose as my offering."

sentences.zh: 」其鵝黃金鑄成，其高七尺，中可實酒三斛。

translations.literal: The goose was cast of gold, seven feet high, and could hold three hu of wine within.
translations.idiomatic: The goose was cast in gold, stood seven feet tall, and could hold three hu of wine within its body.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，右衛率府長史王玄策使往西域，為中天竺所掠。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year, Chief Clerk Wang Xuance of the Right Guard Command was sent on mission to the Western Regions and was plundered by Central India.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year Wang Xuance, chief clerk of the Right Guard Command, was sent to the Western Regions and was robbed by the king of Central India.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃發精兵與玄策擊天竺，大破之，遣使來獻捷。

translations.literal: Tubo sent elite troops to join Xuance in attacking India and inflicted a great defeat, then dispatched envoys to present news of victory.
translations.idiomatic: Tubo sent crack troops to fight beside Xuance against India, routed the enemy, and dispatched envoys to report the victory at court.

sentences.zh: 高宗嗣位，授弄贊為駙馬都尉，封西海郡王，賜物二千段。

translations.literal: When Gaozong succeeded to the throne, he appointed Nongzan Commandant-escort of the Princess and enfeoffed him as Prince of Xihai, bestowing two thousand lengths of goods.
translations.idiomatic: On Gaozong's accession he named Nongzan Commandant-escort of the Princess, enfeoffed him as Prince of the Western Sea, and granted two thousand lengths of silks and goods.

sentences.zh: 弄贊因致書於司徒長孫無忌等云：「天子初即位，若臣下有不忠之心者，當勒兵以赴國除討。

translations.literal: Nongzan therefore sent a letter to the Minister of State Changsun Wuji and others, saying: "The Son of Heaven has just taken the throne; should any minister harbor disloyal intent, I shall marshal troops and come to the state's aid to purge and punish them."
translations.idiomatic: Nongzan wrote to Minister of State Changsun Wuji and others: "Now that the Son of Heaven has newly ascended, should any subject prove disloyal, I shall lead my armies to aid the throne in rooting them out."

sentences.zh: 」並獻金銀珠寶十五種，請置太宗靈座之前。

translations.literal: He also presented fifteen kinds of gold, silver, and jewels, requesting that they be placed before Taizong's spirit seat.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent fifteen kinds of gold, silver, and jewels, asking that they be set before Taizong's spirit tablet.

sentences.zh: 高宗嘉之，進封為賓王，賜雜彩三千段。

translations.literal: Gaozong commended this and advanced his enfeoffment to Prince Bin, granting three thousand lengths of variegated silks.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong was pleased and raised his title to Prince Bin, bestowing three thousand lengths of colored silks.

sentences.zh: 因請蠶種及造酒、碾、硙、紙、墨之匠，並許焉。

translations.literal: He then requested silkworm eggs and craftsmen skilled in making wine, mills, querns, paper, and ink—all were granted.
translations.idiomatic: He also petitioned for silkworm eggs and artisans who knew how to brew wine, run mills and querns, and make paper and ink; all were granted.

sentences.zh: 乃刊石像其形，列昭陵玄闕之下。

translations.literal: A stone image of his likeness was then carved and set below the dark gate of Zhaoling.
translations.idiomatic: A stone statue bearing his likeness was carved and placed below the spirit gate of Zhaoling.

sentences.zh: 永徽元年，弄贊卒。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yonghui, Nongzan died.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yonghui, Nongzan died.

sentences.zh: 高宗為之舉哀，遣右武候將軍鮮于臣濟持節賫璽書吊祭。

translations.literal: Gaozong mourned for him, sending Right Martial Guard general Xianyu Chenji with credentials of office bearing the imperial seal to offer condolences.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong observed mourning on his behalf and sent Xianyu Chenji of the Right Martial Guard with sealed credentials to offer condolences.

sentences.zh: 弄贊子早死，其孫繼立，復號贊普，時年幼，國事皆委祿東贊。

translations.literal: Nongzan's son had died young; his grandson succeeded to the throne and again took the title zanpu. While still a child, all state affairs were entrusted to Gar Tongtsen.
translations.idiomatic: Nongzan's son had died young; his grandson succeeded as zanpu while still a boy, and Gar Tongtsen was entrusted with all affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 祿東姓MS氏，雖不識文記，而性明毅嚴重，講兵訓師，雅有節制，吐蕃之並諸羌，雄霸本土，多其謀也。

translations.literal: Gar Tongtsen's surname was the Gar clan; though he could not read written records, his nature was clear, resolute, and stern. He lectured on warfare and trained troops with proper discipline; that Tubo annexed the various Qiang and dominated its homeland owed much to his stratagems.
translations.idiomatic: Gar Tongtsen belonged to the Gar clan. Though illiterate, he was shrewd, resolute, and grave in bearing; he drilled the army with disciplined method. Much of Tubo's subjugation of the Qiang and dominance of the plateau was his doing.

sentences.zh: 初，太宗既許降文成公主，贊普使祿東贊來迎，召見顧問，進對合旨，太宗禮之，有異諸蕃，乃拜祿東贊為右衛大將軍，又以瑯邪長公主外孫女段氏妻之。

translations.literal: Earlier, after Taizong had agreed to give Princess Wencheng in marriage, the zanpu sent Gar Tongtsen to welcome her. Summoned for audience and counsel, his replies accorded with the emperor's intent; Taizong honored him above other foreign states and appointed Gar Tongtsen Right Guard general, also giving him in marriage Lady Duan, granddaughter by a daughter of the Princess of Langye.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong had agreed to wed Princess Wencheng to the zanpu, Gar Tongtsen came to escort her. Called before the throne, his answers pleased the emperor; Taizong treated him with distinction above all other barbarian envoys, made him Right Guard general, and gave him Lady Duan, a granddaughter of the Princess of Langye, as wife.

sentences.zh: 祿東贊辭曰：「臣本國有婦，父母所聘，情不忍乖。

translations.literal: Gar Tongtsen declined, saying: "Your servant already has a wife in my native state, betrothed by my parents; in feeling I cannot bear to forsake her."
translations.idiomatic: Gar Tongtsen declined: "I already have a wife at home, betrothed by my parents; I cannot in conscience abandon her."

sentences.zh: 且贊普未謁公主，陪臣安敢輒娶。

translations.literal: Moreover, the zanpu has not yet met the princess; how dare a companion minister presume to marry first?"
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the zanpu has not yet received the princess; how dare a mere attendant minister marry before him?"

sentences.zh: 」太宗嘉之，欲撫以厚恩，雖奇其答而不遂其請。

translations.literal: Taizong commended this and wished to comfort him with generous favor; though he marveled at the reply, he did not grant the marriage request.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong admired his reply and meant to reward him generously, but though struck by his answer he did not press the marriage.

sentences.zh: 祿東贊有子五人：長曰贊悉若，早死；

translations.literal: Gar Tongtsen had five sons: the eldest was Zanxinuo, who died young;
translations.idiomatic: Gar Tongtsen had five sons. The eldest, Zanxinuo, died young;

sentences.zh: 次欽陵，次贊婆，次悉多幹，次勃論。

translations.literal: next Qinling, next Zanpo, next Xiduogan, and last Bolun.
translations.idiomatic: then Qinling, then Zanpo, then Xiduogan, and lastly Bolun.

sentences.zh: 及東贊死，欽陵兄弟復專其國。

translations.literal: When Gar Tongtsen died, Qinling and his brothers again monopolized control of the state.
translations.idiomatic: After Gar Tongtsen's death, Qinling and his brothers once more seized control of the realm.

sentences.zh: 後與吐谷渾不和，龍朔、麟德中遞相表奏，各論曲直，國家依違，未為與奪。

translations.literal: Later they fell out with Tuyuhun; during Longshuo and Linde each side sent memorials in turn arguing right and wrong, and the court wavered without deciding for either.
translations.idiomatic: They later quarreled with Tuyuhun; through the Longshuo and Linde years each side petitioned the court with its case, but the throne hesitated and rendered no judgment.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃怨怒，遂率兵以擊吐谷渾。

translations.literal: Tubo, resentful and angry, then led troops to attack Tuyuhun.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, Tubo marched against Tuyuhun.

sentences.zh: 吐谷渾大敗，河源王慕容諾曷缽及弘化公主脫身走投涼州，遣使告急。

translations.literal: Tuyuhun suffered a great defeat; the Prince of Heyuan Murong Nuohubo and Princess Honghua escaped and fled to Liangzhou, sending envoys to report the emergency.
translations.idiomatic: Tuyuhun was routed; Murong Nuohubo, Prince of Heyuan, and Princess Honghua fled to Liang Prefecture and sent envoys begging for aid.

sentences.zh: 上元三年，進寇鄯、廓等州，殺掠人吏，高宗命尚書左僕射劉仁軌往洮河軍鎮守以禦之。

translations.literal: In the third year of Shangyuan they advanced to raid Shan, Kuo, and other prefectures, killing and plundering officials and people. Gaozong ordered Left Vice Minister of State Liu Rengui to go to the Taohe army to garrison and defend against them.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Shangyuan they raided Shan, Kuo, and neighboring prefectures, slaughtering officials and civilians alike. Gaozong sent Liu Rengui, Left Vice Minister of State, to hold the Taohe garrison against them.

sentences.zh: 儀鳳三年，又命中書令李敬玄兼鄯州都督，往代仁軌於洮河鎮守。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yifeng he again appointed Chief Councilor Li Jingxuan concurrently Protector-general of Shanzhou to replace Rengui in garrisoning the Taohe.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yifeng he appointed Chief Councilor Li Jingxuan concurrent protector of Shan Prefecture to relieve Rengui on the Taohe line.

sentences.zh: 仍召募關內、河東及諸州驍勇，以為猛士，不簡色役。

translations.literal: He also recruited fierce warriors from Guannei, Hedong, and various prefectures to serve as crack troops, without regard to corvée status.
translations.idiomatic: Crack fighters were recruited from Guannei, Hedong, and the provinces without regard to corvée obligations.

sentences.zh: 亦有嘗任文武官者召入殿庭賜宴，遣往擊之。

translations.literal: Some who had formerly held civil or military office were summoned to the palace hall for a feast and then sent to attack the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Former civil and military officials were summoned to court, feasted, and dispatched to the front.

sentences.zh: 又令益州長史李孝逸、巂州都督拓王奉等發劍南、山南兵募以防禦之。

translations.literal: He also ordered Chief Clerk of Yizhou Li Xiaoyi, Protector-general of Qizhou Tuowang Feng, and others to raise levies from Jiannan and Shannan troops for defense.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiaoyi, chief clerk of Yizhou, Tuowang Feng, protector of Qizhou, and others were ordered to raise troops from Jiannan and Shannan for the defense.

sentences.zh: 其年秋，敬玄與工部尚書劉審禮，率兵與吐蕃戰於青海。

translations.literal: That autumn Jingxuan and Minister of Works Liu Shenli led troops to fight Tubo at Qinghai.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn Li Jingxuan and Liu Shenli, Minister of Works, led the army against the Tibetans at Qinghai.

sentences.zh: 官軍敗積，審禮沒於陣，敬玄按軍不敢救。

translations.literal: The government army was badly defeated; Shenli perished in the battle line, and Jingxuan held his troops back and dared not rescue him.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang army was routed; Shenli fell on the field while Jingxuan held his men back and dared not go to his aid.

sentences.zh: 俄而收軍卻出，頓於承風嶺，阻泥溝不能動，賊屯於高岡以壓之。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he gathered the army and withdrew, encamping at Chengfeng Ridge; blocked by muddy ravines they could not move, while the enemy held the high hills to press them down.
translations.idiomatic: He soon gathered the remnants and withdrew to Chengfeng Ridge, where muddy gullies pinned them in place while the enemy held the heights above.

sentences.zh: 偏將左領軍員外將軍黑齒常之率敢死之士五百人，夜斫賊營，賊遂潰亂，自相蹂踐，死者三百余人。

translations.literal: Deputy general, Left Army Inspector Outside General Heichi Changzhi led five hundred dare-to-die troops and at night struck the enemy camp; the enemy then broke in disorder, trampling one another, and more than three hundred died.
translations.idiomatic: The deputy commander Heichi Changzhi, Left Army Inspector Outside General, led five hundred volunteers in a night attack on the enemy camp. The foe broke and fled in chaos, trampling one another; over three hundred perished.

sentences.zh: 敬玄遂擁眾鄯州，坐改為衡州刺史。

translations.literal: Jingxuan then led his forces to Shanzhou; on that account he was demoted to prefect of Hengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jingxuan withdrew with his army to Shanzhou and, as punishment, was reassigned as prefect of Hengzhou.

sentences.zh: 往劍南兵募，於茂州之西南築安戎城以壓其境。

translations.literal: Troops were levied from Jiannan, and southwest of Maozhou they built Ancheng Fort to press upon their territory.
translations.idiomatic: Levies were raised in Jiannan, and Ancheng Fort was built southwest of Maozhou to bear down on the Tubo frontier.

sentences.zh: 俄有生羌為吐蕃鄉導，攻陷其城，遂引兵守之。

translations.literal: Before long living Qiang acted as guides for Tubo, attacked and took the fort, then led troops to hold it.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward local Qiang served Tubo as guides, stormed the fort, and garrisoned it with their troops.

sentences.zh: 時吐蕃盡收羊同、党項及諸羌之地，東與涼、松、茂、巂等州相接，南至婆羅門，西又攻陷龜茲、疏勒等四鎮，北抵突厥，地方萬餘里，自漢、魏已來，西戎之盛，未之有也。

translations.literal: At that time Tubo had fully taken the lands of Yangtong, the Tangut, and the various Qiang; east they adjoined Liang, Song, Mao, Xi, and other prefectures; south to Brahman; west they also attacked and took the four garrisons of Kucha, Kashgar, and the rest; north reaching the Turks—territory of more than ten thousand li. Since Han and Wei times, no western barbarian power had been so great.
translations.idiomatic: Tubo had absorbed Yangtong, the Tangut, and the Qiang peoples. Its eastern marches bordered Liang, Song, Mao, Xi, and neighboring prefectures; to the south it reached Brahman lands; to the west it seized Kucha, Kashgar, and the other four garrisons; to the north it pressed the Turks—a realm of more than ten thousand li. Since Han and Wei, no power of the western barbarians had matched it.

sentences.zh: 高宗聞審禮等敗沒，召侍臣問綏禦之策，中書舍人郭正一曰：「吐蕃作梗，年歲已深，命將興師，相繼不絕。

translations.literal: Gaozong heard that Shenli and the others were defeated and lost, summoned attendant ministers to ask policy for pacification and defense; Secretariat drafting courtier Guo Zhengyi said: "Tubo causes obstruction; the years have already grown deep; ordering generals and raising armies has continued without cease.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozong learned of Liu Shenli's defeat and death, he called his close advisers to discuss border policy. Guo Zhengyi, drafting courtier of the Secretariat, said: "Tubo has been our scourge for many years, and campaign after campaign has been launched without pause.

sentences.zh: 空勞士馬，虛費糧儲，近討則徒損兵威，深入則未窮巢穴，望少發兵募，且遣備邊，明烽堠，勿令侵抄。

translations.literal: In vain tiring soldiers and horses, wasting grain stores; near expedition then only damages military prestige, deep penetration still does not reach their nest—Your Majesty should send few levy troops and instead strengthen border defense, make beacon towers clear, and not let them raid and plunder.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers and horses are worn out in vain, and stores are squandered. A shallow strike only wastes our prestige; a deep thrust still fails to destroy their lair. I beg that levies be kept small, that the frontier be fortified, beacons kept bright, and raids forbidden.

sentences.zh: 使國用豐足，人心葉同，寬之數年，可一舉而滅。

translations.literal: Make state expenditures ample and the people's hearts turn as one; give them several years' reprieve and they can be destroyed in one stroke.
translations.idiomatic: Let the treasury grow full and the people stand united; after a few years of forbearance, we may annihilate them at a single blow.

sentences.zh: 」給事中劉齊賢、皇甫文亮等皆言嚴守之便。

translations.literal: " Attendant within the Secretariat Liu Qixian, Huangfu Wenliang, and others all said strict defense was the better course.
translations.idiomatic: " Liu Qixian, Huangfu Wenliang, and other remonstrance officials all urged that a firm defensive posture was best.

sentences.zh: 尋而黑齒常之破吐蕃大將贊婆及素和貴於良非川，殺獲二千余級，吐蕃遂引退。

translations.literal: Soon Heichi Changzhi defeated Tubo great generals Zanpo and Suhe Gui at Liangfei River, killed and captured more than two thousand heads, and Tubo then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Heichi Changzhi routed the Tubo commanders Zanpo and Suhe Gui at Liangfei River, killing and capturing more than two thousand men, and Tubo withdrew.

sentences.zh: 詔以常之為河源軍使以鎮禦之。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Changzhi Heyuan Army commissioner to defend against them.
translations.idiomatic: Changzhi was appointed commissioner of the Heyuan Army to guard the frontier against Tubo.

sentences.zh: 則天臨朝，命文昌右相韋待價為安息道大總管，安西大都護閻溫古為副。

translations.literal: When Wuzetian held court, she ordered Right Vice Minister of the Secretariat Wei Daijia as Grand Marshal of the Anxi Circuit and Western Regions Grand Protector Yan Wengu as deputy.
translations.idiomatic: After Wuzetian took power, she named Wei Daijia, Right Vice Minister of the Secretariat, Grand Marshal of the Anxi Circuit, with Yan Wengu, Grand Protector of the Western Regions, as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 永昌元年，率兵往征吐蕃，遲留不進，待價坐流浦州，溫古處斬。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongchang she led troops to campaign against Tubo; they delayed and did not advance—Daijia was sentenced to exile in Puzhou and Wengu was executed.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongchang the army marched against Tubo but stalled on the road. Wei Daijia was banished to Puzhou; Yan Wengu was put to death.

sentences.zh: 待價素無統禦之才，遂狼狽失據，士卒饑饉，皆轉死溝壑。

translations.literal: Daijia had never possessed talent for command; thus in disarray he lost his footing, the soldiers starved, and all turned to die in ditches and gullies.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Daijia had no gift for command. His army fell apart in disorder; the men starved and perished by the thousands in gullies and ravines.

sentences.zh: 明年，又命文昌右相岑長倩為武威道行軍大總管以討吐蕃，中路退還，軍竟不行。

translations.literal: The next year she again ordered Right Vice Minister Cen Changqian as Mobile Grand Marshal of the Wuwei Circuit to attack Tubo; midway he returned, and the army in the end did not march.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Cen Changqian, Right Vice Minister of the Secretariat, was made Mobile Grand Marshal of the Wuwei Circuit against Tubo, but he turned back en route and the expedition never took the field.

sentences.zh: 如意元年，吐蕃大首領曷蘇率其所屬並貴川部落請降，則天令右玉鈐衛大將軍張玄遇率精卒二萬充安撫使以納之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Ruyi, Tubo great chieftain Hasu led his subordinates and the Bingguichuan tribes to request surrender; Wuzetian ordered Right Jade Bell Guard General Zhang Xuan'yu to lead twenty thousand elite troops as pacification commissioner to receive them.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Ruyi the Tubo chieftain Hasu led his followers and the Bingguichuan clans in offering submission. Wuzetian sent Zhang Xuan'yu of the Right Jade Bell Guard with twenty thousand picked troops as pacification commissioner to accept them.

sentences.zh: 師次大渡水，曷蘇事泄，為本國所擒，又有大首領昝捶率羌蠻部落八千余人詣玄遇內附。

translations.literal: The army halted at the Dadu River; Hasu's affair was exposed and he was seized by his own state; also great chieftain Zanchui led Qiang and barbarian tribes of more than eight thousand to Xuan'yu to submit.
translations.idiomatic: When the column reached the Dadu River, Hasu's plot was discovered and his countrymen seized him. Another chieftain, Zanchui, then led more than eight thousand Qiang and tribal followers to Zhang Xuan'yu to surrender.

sentences.zh: 玄遇以其部落置葉川州，以昝捶為刺史。

translations.literal: Xuan'yu settled their tribe in Yechuan Prefecture and made Zanchui prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xuan'yu established Yechuan Prefecture for the tribe and appointed Zanchui its prefect.

sentences.zh: 仍於大度西山勒石紀功而還。

translations.literal: He also carved stone on the western mountains of Dadu to record his achievement and returned.
translations.idiomatic: On the western hills of the Dadu he set up a stone inscription commemorating the victory, then marched home.

sentences.zh: 長壽元年，武威軍總管王孝傑大破吐蕃之眾，克復龜茲、於闐、疏勒、碎葉等四鎮，乃於龜茲置安西都護府，發兵以鎮守之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Changshou, Wuwei Army Inspector Wang Xiaojie greatly defeated the Tubo host, recovered the four garrisons of Kucha, Khotan, Kashgar, and Suyab, then at Kucha established the Anxi Protectorate and sent troops to garrison it.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Changshou, Wang Xiaojie, inspector of the Wuwei Army, routed the Tubo forces and retook Kucha, Khotan, Kashgar, and Suyab. He re-established the Anxi Protectorate at Kucha and posted troops to hold the region.

sentences.zh: 萬歲登封元年，孝傑復為肅邊道大總管，率副總管婁師德與吐蕃將論欽陵、贊婆戰於素羅汗山。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wansui Dengfeng, Xiaojie again became Grand Marshal of the Subi Border Circuit, leading Deputy Grand Marshal Lou Shide to fight the Tubo generals Gar Tongtsen and Zanpo at Mount Suluohan.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Wansui Dengfeng, Wang Xiaojie was again made Grand Marshal of the Subi Border Circuit. With Deputy Grand Marshal Lou Shide he met the Tubo generals Gar Tongtsen and Zanpo at Mount Suluohan.

sentences.zh: 官軍敗績，李傑坐免官。

translations.literal: The government army was defeated; Wang Xiaojie was dismissed from office on that account.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang army was routed, and Wang Xiaojie was removed from his post.

sentences.zh: 萬歲通天元年，吐蕃四萬眾奄至涼州城下，都督許欽明初不之覺，輕出按部，遂遇賊，拒戰久之，力屈為賊所殺。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wansui Tongtian, forty thousand Tubo troops suddenly reached below Liangzhou city; Protector Xu Qinming at first did not notice, went out lightly to inspect his district, met the enemy, resisted a long time, his strength gave way, and he was killed by the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Wansui Tongtian forty thousand Tubo soldiers appeared before Liangzhou. Protector Xu Qinming, unaware at first, rode out on a routine inspection, ran into the raiders, fought long but was overcome, and fell in battle.

sentences.zh: 時吐蕃又遣使請和，則天將許之；

translations.literal: At that time Tubo also sent envoys seeking peace, and Wuzetian was about to agree;
translations.idiomatic: Tubo then sent envoys suing for peace, and Wuzetian was inclined to grant it;

sentences.zh: 論欽陵乃請去安西四鎮兵，仍索分十姓之地，則天竟不許之。

translations.literal: Gar Tongtsen then requested withdrawal of the Anxi Four Garrisons' troops and still demanded a share of the Ten Surnames' lands; Wuzetian in the end did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: but Gar Tongtsen demanded the withdrawal of Tang garrisons from the Four Protectorates of Anxi and a partition of the Ten Surnames' territory. Wuzetian refused.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃自論欽陵兄弟專統兵馬，欽陵每居中用事，諸弟分據方面，贊婆則專在東境，與中國為鄰，三十余年，常為邊患。

translations.literal: From the time Gar Tongtsen and his brothers monopolized military affairs, Qinling often held power at the center while the younger brothers each held their regions; Zanpo then held the eastern marches alone, adjoining China—for more than thirty years they were a constant border calamity.
translations.idiomatic: After Gar Tongtsen and his brothers seized control of Tubo's armies, Qinling usually directed affairs from the center while his brothers held the provinces; Zanpo guarded the eastern frontier against Tang for more than thirty years, a perennial scourge on the border.

sentences.zh: 其兄弟皆有才略，諸蕃憚之。

translations.literal: The brothers all possessed talent and stratagem; the various barbarians feared them.
translations.idiomatic: All the brothers were gifted strategists, and the surrounding peoples stood in awe of them.

sentences.zh: 聖歷二年，其贊普器弩悉弄年漸長，乃與其大臣論巖等密圖之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shengl, their zanpu Tridu Songtsen gradually grew older; he and his great minister Lun Yan and others secretly plotted against them.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Shengl their zanpu Tridu Songtsen came of age and, with the minister Lun Yan and others, laid secret plans against the Gar clan.

sentences.zh: 時欽陵在外，贊普乃佯言將獵，召兵執欽陵親黨二千余人，殺之。

translations.literal: At that time Gar Tongtsen was abroad; the zanpu then feigned a hunting expedition, summoned troops, seized more than two thousand of Gar Tongtsen's intimates, and killed them.
translations.idiomatic: Gar Tongtsen was away at the time. The zanpu pretended to go hunting, called up troops, and arrested and executed more than two thousand of Gar Tongtsen's partisans.

sentences.zh: 發使召欽陵、贊婆等，欽陵舉兵不受召，贊普自帥眾討之，欽陵未戰而潰，遂自殺，其親信左右同日自殺者百余人。

translations.literal: He sent messengers to summon Gar Tongtsen, Zanpo, and the rest; Gar Tongtsen raised troops and did not obey the summons; the zanpu personally led forces to attack him; Gar Tongtsen collapsed without fighting, then killed himself; on the same day more than a hundred of his trusted attendants also killed themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys were sent to summon Gar Tongtsen and Zanpo, but Gar Tongtsen refused and took up arms. The zanpu marched against him in person. Gar Tongtsen's host melted away without a battle; he took his own life, and more than a hundred of his closest followers died with him that same day.

sentences.zh: 贊婆率所部千余人及其兄子莽布支等來降，則天遣羽林飛騎郊外迎之，授贊婆輔國大將軍、行右衛大將軍，封歸德郡王，優賜甚厚，仍令領其部兵於洪源谷討擊。

translations.literal: Zanpo led his division of more than a thousand men and his brother's son Mangbuzhi and others to surrender; Wuzetian sent Feathered Forest Rapid Cavalry to welcome them outside the suburbs, appointed Zanpo Assistant State Grand General and acting Right Guard Grand General, enfeoffed him Prince of Guide Commandery with very generous gifts, and still ordered him to lead his tribal troops at Hongyuangu to strike the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Zanpo came over with more than a thousand followers and his nephew Mangbuzhi. Wuzetian sent the Feathered Forest Rapid Cavalry to meet them beyond the walls, made Zanpo Assistant State Grand General and acting Right Guard Grand General, created him Prince of Guide Commandery with rich rewards, and set him to lead his men against Tubo from Hongyuangu.

sentences.zh: 尋卒，贈特進、安西大都護。

translations.literal: Soon he died; posthumously he was promoted Special Advance and Western Regions Grand Protector.
translations.idiomatic: He died not long after. Posthumously he was honored as Special Advance and Grand Protector of the Western Regions.

sentences.zh: 時吐蕃南境屬國泥婆羅門等皆叛，贊普自往討之，卒於軍中。

translations.literal: At that time Tubo's southern tributaries, including Nepal and others, all rebelled; the zanpu personally went to attack them and died in the army.
translations.idiomatic: Tubo's southern vassals, including Nepal, rose in revolt. The zanpu led the campaign in person and died on campaign.

sentences.zh: 諸子爭立，久之，國人立器弩悉弄之子棄隸蹜贊為贊普，時年七歲。

translations.literal: Sons struggled for the throne; after a long time the people established Tridu Songtsen's son Mangsong Mangtsen as zanpu; he was then seven years old.
translations.idiomatic: His sons fought over the succession. Eventually the realm enthroned Tridu Songtsen's son Mangsong Mangtsen as zanpu at the age of seven.

sentences.zh: 中宗神龍元年，吐蕃使來告喪，中宗為之舉哀，廢朝一日。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shenlong of Zhongzong, Tubo envoys came to announce the mourning; Zhongzong held mourning for him and suspended court for one day.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Shenlong, Tubo envoys announced the zanpu's death. Zhongzong observed mourning and closed court for a day.

sentences.zh: 俄而贊普之祖母遣其大臣悉薰然來獻方物，為其孫請婚，中宗以所養雍王守禮女為金城公主許嫁之。

translations.literal: Before long the zanpu's grandmother sent her great minister Xixiran to present local products and request marriage for her grandson; Zhongzong betrothed the daughter he was raising, the child of Prince Yong the Defending, as Princess Jincheng to marry him.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the zanpu's grandmother dispatched the minister Xixiran with gifts and a request to wed her grandson. Zhongzong gave him the girl he had raised—the daughter of Prince Yong, Defender of the Realm—as Princess Jincheng.

sentences.zh: 自是頻歲貢獻。

translations.literal: From this they presented tribute every year.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter Tubo sent tribute annually.

sentences.zh: 景龍三年十一月，又遣其大臣尚贊吐等來迎女，中宗宴之於苑內球場，命駙馬都尉楊慎交與吐蕃使打球，中宗率侍臣觀之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the third year of Jinglong they again sent the great minister Shangzan Tu and others to welcome the princess; Zhongzong feasted them in the garden polo ground, ordered the emperor's son-in-law Commandant Yang Shenjiao and the Tubo envoys to play polo, and Zhongzong led attendant ministers to watch.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the third year of Jinglong Tubo again sent Shangzan Tu and other ministers to escort the bride. Zhongzong entertained them at the palace polo grounds, had Commandant Yang Shenjiao play ball against the Tubo envoys, and watched with his court.

sentences.zh: 四年正月，制曰：

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the fourth year an edict said:
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fourth year an edict proclaimed:

sentences.zh: 聖人布化，用百姓為心；

translations.literal: The sage spreads transformation, taking the hundred surnames as his heart;
translations.idiomatic: The sage-king transforms the realm with the welfare of the people as his heart;

sentences.zh: 王者垂仁，以八荒無外。

translations.literal: The king suspends benevolence, with the eight wilds without anything outside.
translations.idiomatic: the king extends his grace until nothing beyond the eight directions lies outside his care.

sentences.zh: 故能光宅遐邇，裁成品物。

translations.literal: Thus he can illuminate the near and far and trim and complete the myriad things.
translations.idiomatic: Thus his light reaches near and far, and the myriad things are brought to their proper form.

sentences.zh: 由是隆周理歷，恢柔遠之圖；

translations.literal: Hence the Zhou flourished in ordering the calendar and broadened the plan of cherishing the distant;
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou in its glory ordered the seasons and widened its policy of cherishing distant peoples;

sentences.zh: 強漢乘時，建和親之議。

translations.literal: the strong Han seized the moment and established the policy of marriage alliance.
translations.idiomatic: the mighty Han seized its hour and founded the policy of marriage alliances.

sentences.zh: 斯蓋宇長策，經邦茂範。

translations.literal: This is truly a long-range stratagem and a flourishing model for governing the state.
translations.idiomatic: Such measures are a lasting strategy and a splendid model for ruling the realm.

sentences.zh: 朕受命上靈，克纂洪業，庶幾前烈，永致和平。

translations.literal: We have received the mandate from the highest spirits, succeeded to the great enterprise, and hope to match the former achievements and bring peace forever.
translations.idiomatic: We have received Heaven's mandate, inherited a great patrimony, and aspire to equal the achievements of old and secure lasting peace.

sentences.zh: 睠彼吐蕃，僻在西服，皇運之始，早申朝貢。

translations.literal: Regarding that Tubo, remote in the western lands, from the beginning of our dynasty's fortune they early offered court tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Tubo lies remote in the western marches; from the dawn of our fortune they have long paid court tribute.

sentences.zh: 太宗文武聖皇帝德侔覆載，情深億兆，思偃兵甲，遂通姻好，數十年間，一方清凈。

translations.literal: Taizong the Civil and Martial Sagely Emperor's virtue matched heaven and earth covering all; his feeling for the hundred million was deep; he wished to lay down arms and armor and thus opened marriage ties; for several tens of years one region was pure and still.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong, civil and martial sage, whose virtue covered heaven and earth and whose care embraced the myriad people, sought to sheathe the sword and joined his house to theirs in marriage; for decades the frontier knew quiet.

sentences.zh: 自文成公主化往，其國因多變革。

translations.literal: Since Princess Wencheng passed away, their state has undergone many changes.
translations.idiomatic: After Princess Wencheng's death their realm fell into repeated turmoil.

sentences.zh: 我之邊隅，亟興師旅，彼之蕃落，頗聞雕弊。

translations.literal: On our borderlands armies have been raised again and again; among their tribal settlements exhaustion has been widely heard.
translations.idiomatic: Our borders have seen campaign after campaign; among their tribesmen hardship is widely reported.

sentences.zh: 頃者贊普及祖母可敦、酋長等，屢披誠款，積有歲時，思托舊親，請崇新好。

translations.literal: Recently the zanpu together with the Grand Lady, chieftains, and others have repeatedly shown sincere intent for many years, desiring to rely on the old kinship and request renewed friendship.
translations.idiomatic: Lately the zanpu, the Grand Lady, and their chiefs have for years pressed their sincere wish to renew the old kinship and bind a fresh peace.

sentences.zh: 金城公主，朕之少女，豈不鐘念，但為人父母，誌息黎元，若允乃誠祈，更敦和好，則邊土寧晏，兵役服息。

translations.literal: Princess Jincheng is Our young daughter—how could We not cherish her? Yet as parents of the people, Our aim is to give the black-haired masses rest; if We grant their sincere prayer and further thicken good relations, then the borderlands will be tranquil and military service will cease.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Jincheng is Our own young daughter, and Our heart is not unmoved; yet as father and mother of the people We seek repose for the common folk. If We honor their earnest plea and renew amity, the frontier will be calm and the armies may stand down.

sentences.zh: 遂割深慈，為國大計，築茲外館，聿膺嘉禮，降彼吐蕃贊普，即以今月進發，朕想自送於郊外。

translations.literal: We therefore set aside deep parental feeling for the great plan of the state, built this outer lodge, and undertook the auspicious rite; she descends to wed the Tubo zanpu and sets out this very month—We intend to escort her personally beyond the suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: We have therefore sacrificed private affection to the needs of the realm, raised this outer lodge, and accepted the wedding rites. The princess goes forth this month to wed the Tubo zanpu, and We mean to see her off beyond the city ourselves.

sentences.zh: 中宗召侍中紀處訥謂曰：「昔文成公主出降，則江夏王送之。

translations.literal: Zhongzong summoned Attendant within the Secretariat Ji Chune and said to him: "In former times when Princess Wencheng went out in marriage, the Prince of Jiangxia escorted her.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzong called in Ji Chune, Attendant within the Secretariat, and said: "When Princess Wencheng was sent to marry, the Prince of Jiangxia escorted her.

sentences.zh: 卿雅識蕃情，有安邊之略，可為朕充吐蕃使也。

translations.literal: You are well versed in Tubo affairs and possess strategy for securing the border; you may serve Us as envoy to Tubo."
translations.idiomatic: You know Tubo well and have a plan for securing the frontier. Go as Our envoy to Tubo."

sentences.zh: 」處訥拜謝，既而以不練邊事固辭。

translations.literal: " Chune bowed in thanks, then on the ground of being unskilled in border affairs firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: Chune thanked him but declined on the ground that he was unversed in frontier matters.

sentences.zh: 上又令中書侍郎趙彥昭充使。

translations.literal: The emperor again ordered Secretariat Vice Director Zhao Yanzhao to serve as envoy.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then named Zhao Yanzhao, Vice Director of the Secretariat, envoy in his stead.

sentences.zh: 彥昭以既充外使，恐失其權寵，殊不悅。

translations.literal: Yanzhao, because he had already been made foreign envoy, feared losing his favor and power, and was very displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhao was displeased, fearing that service abroad would cost him influence at court.

sentences.zh: 司農卿趙履溫私謂之曰：「公國之宰輔，而為一介之使，不亦鄙乎？

translations.literal: Minister of Imperial Granaries Zhao Lüwen privately said to him: "You are a chief minister of the state, yet you become a mere envoy—is it not contemptible?
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Lüwen, Minister of Imperial Granaries, took him aside and said: "You stand among the chief ministers of the realm—will you go as a simple courier? Is that not beneath your station?

sentences.zh: 」彥昭曰：「然計將安出？

translations.literal: " Yanzhao said: "Yet what plan shall we devise?"
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhao asked: "Then what is to be done?"

sentences.zh: 」履溫因陰托安樂公主密奏留之。

translations.literal: " Lüwen then secretly had Princess Anle memorialize to keep him.
translations.idiomatic: Lüwen secretly persuaded Princess Anle to memorialize the throne and have him retained.

sentences.zh: 於是以左衛大將軍楊矩使焉。

translations.literal: Thereupon Left Guard Grand General Yang Ju was sent in his place.
translations.idiomatic: Left Guard Grand General Yang Ju was sent instead.

sentences.zh: 其月，帝幸始平縣以送公主，設帳殿於百頃泊側，引王公宰相及吐蕃使入宴，中坐酒闌，命吐蕃使進前，諭以公主孩幼，割慈遠嫁之旨，上悲泣歔欷久之。

translations.literal: That month the emperor visited Shiping County to escort the princess, pitched a tent hall beside Baiqing Marsh, led princes, dukes, chancellors, and Tubo envoys in to feast; when the wine was halfway through he ordered the Tubo envoy to come forward and expounded the meaning that the princess was young and was being sent far in severance of parental affection; the emperor wept and sobbed a long time.
translations.idiomatic: That month the emperor traveled to Shiping County to see the princess off. A tent-pavilion was set beside Baiqing Marsh, and princes, ministers, and Tubo envoys were brought to feast. Midway through the wine he called the Tubo envoy forward and spoke of the princess's youth and the pain of parting; the emperor wept long and bitterly.

sentences.zh: 因命從臣賦詩餞別，曲赦始平縣大辟罪已下，百姓給復一年，改始平縣為金城縣，又改其地為鳳池鄉愴別裏。

translations.literal: He then ordered attendant ministers to compose poems for the farewell, granted a general amnesty in Shiping County for capital crimes and below, gave the people tax relief for one year, changed Shiping County to Jincheng County, and changed its land to Fengchi Township, Village of Sorrowful Parting.
translations.idiomatic: He bade his courtiers compose parting poems, pardoned all crimes short of capital offense in Shiping, exempted the people from taxes for a year, renamed the county Jincheng, and called the place Fengchi Township, "Lane of Mourning Farewell."

sentences.zh: 公主既至吐蕃，別築一城以居之。

translations.literal: After the princess reached Tubo, they built a separate city for her to dwell in.
translations.idiomatic: When the princess arrived in Tubo, a separate city was built for her residence.

sentences.zh: 睿宗即位，攝監察御史李知古上言：「姚州諸蠻，先屬吐蕃，請發兵擊之。

translations.literal: When Ruizong took the throne, Acting Investigating Censor Li Zhigu memorialized: "The various Man of Yaozhou formerly belonged to Tubo; please send troops to attack them."
translations.idiomatic: At Ruizong's accession the acting investigating censor Li Zhigu submitted: "The tribal peoples of Yaozhou once owed allegiance to Tubo; send troops to strike them."

sentences.zh: 」遂令知古征劍南兵募往經略之。

translations.literal: " He was then ordered to levy Jiannan troops and go to pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhigu was ordered to raise Jiannan levies and march to subdue them.

sentences.zh: 蠻酋傍名乃引吐蕃攻知古，殺之，仍斷其屍以祭天。

translations.literal: The Man chieftain Pangming then led Tubo to attack Zhigu, killed him, and still cut up his corpse to sacrifice to Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The chieftain Pangming brought in Tubo forces, killed Zhigu, and dismembered his body for a sacrifice to Heaven.

sentences.zh: 時張玄表為安西都護，又與吐蕃比境，互相攻掠，吐蕃內雖怨怒，外敦和好。

translations.literal: At that time Zhang Xuanbiao was Protector of Anxi and again shared a border with Tubo; they attacked and plundered one another; within Tubo though there was resentment, outwardly they cultivated good relations.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xuanbiao was then Protector of Anxi; though Tubo and Tang raided each other along the frontier, Tubo outwardly maintained the language of peace even as anger smoldered within.

sentences.zh: 時楊矩為鄯州都督，吐蕃遣使厚遺之，因請河西九曲之地以為金城公主湯沐之所，矩遂奏與之。

translations.literal: At that time Yang Ju was Protector of Shanzhou; Tubo sent envoys with rich gifts to him and thereby requested the land of the Nine Bends of the Hexi as a bath-estate for Princess Jincheng; Ju then memorialized to grant it.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Ju was then Protector of Shanzhou. Tubo envoys brought him lavish gifts and asked for the Nine Bends of the Hexi as Princess Jincheng's fief; Ju memorialized the throne and the land was granted.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃既得九曲，其地肥良，堪頓兵畜牧，又與唐境接近，自是復叛，始率兵入寇。

translations.literal: Tubo having obtained the Nine Bends, the land was fertile and good, suitable for encamping troops and pasturing herds, and again close to Tang territory; from this they rebelled again and first led troops in to raid.
translations.idiomatic: Once Tubo held the Nine Bends, it gained rich pasture for armies and herds and stood hard against Tang territory. They broke faith and again sent raiders across the border.

sentences.zh: 開元二年秋，吐蕃大將闉達焉、乞力徐等率眾十余萬寇臨洮軍，又進寇蘭、渭等州，掠監牧羊馬而去。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the second year of Kaiyuan, Tubo great generals Mindaya, Qilixu, and others led a host of more than a hundred thousand to raid Lintao Army and advanced to raid Lan, Wei, and other prefectures, driving off the supervised herds of sheep and horses and departing.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the second year of Kaiyuan the Tubo generals Mindaya and Qilixu led more than a hundred thousand men against Lintao Army and pressed on into Lan and Wei, carrying off the frontier herds before withdrawing.

sentences.zh: 楊矩悔懼，飲藥而死。

translations.literal: Yang Ju, regretful and afraid, drank poison and died.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Ju, stricken with remorse and fear, took poison and died.

sentences.zh: 玄宗令攝左羽林將軍薛訥及太仆少卿王晙率兵邀擊之。

translations.literal: Xuanzong ordered Acting Left Feathered Forest General Xue Ne and Vice Director of the Imperial Stud Wang Jun to lead troops to intercept and strike them.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong sent the acting Left Feathered Forest General Xue Ne and Wang Jun, Vice Director of the Imperial Stud, to intercept the raiders.

sentences.zh: 仍下詔將大舉親征，召募將士，克期進發。

translations.literal: He also issued an edict that he would personally lead a great campaign, recruiting soldiers with a fixed date for advance.
translations.idiomatic: An edict announced that the emperor would take the field in person, recruiting troops for a set day of march.

sentences.zh: 俄而晙等與賊相遇於渭源之武階驛，前軍王海賓力戰死之，晙等率兵而進，大破吐蕃之眾，殺數萬人，盡收復所掠羊馬。

translations.literal: Before long Jun and the others met the enemy at Wujie Post in the headwaters of the Wei; vanguard Wang Haibin fought fiercely and died; Jun and the others led the army forward and greatly defeated the Tubo host, killing tens of thousands and fully recovering the sheep and horses that had been driven off.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Wang Jun and his colleagues met the enemy at Wujie Post on the Wei headwaters. The vanguard Wang Haibin fought to the death; Jun pressed on and shattered the Tubo army, slaying tens of thousands and recovering all the stolen herds.

sentences.zh: 賊余黨奔北，相枕藉而死，洮水為之不流。

translations.literal: The enemy remnants fled north; they died piled one upon another, and the Tao River did not flow for them.
translations.idiomatic: The survivors fled north, dying in heaps so thick that the Tao River was choked and could not run.

sentences.zh: 上遂罷親征，命紫微舍人倪若水往按軍實，仍吊祭王海賓而還。

translations.literal: The emperor then canceled the personal campaign, ordered Secretariat Drafter Ni Ruoshui to go inspect the army's true condition, and still mourned and sacrificed for Wang Haibin before returning.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor called off his own expedition, sent Ni Ruoshui of the Secretariat to review the army's condition, and performed rites of mourning for Wang Haibin on his behalf.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃遣其大臣宗俄因子至洮河祭其死亡之士，仍款塞請和，不上許之。

translations.literal: Tubo sent its great minister Zong'e Ziyin to the Tao River to sacrifice for its dead soldiers and still came to the border with friendly intent seeking peace; the emperor did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: Tubo sent the minister Zong'e Ziyin to the Tao River to bury its dead and then sued for peace at the border, but the emperor would not agree.

sentences.zh: 自是連年犯邊，郭知運、王君相次為河西節度使以捍之。

translations.literal: From this they violated the border year after year; Guo Zhiyun and Wang Junyi in succession became Hexi military commissioners to defend against them.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter Tubo raided the frontier year after year. Guo Zhiyun and Wang Junyi served in turn as military commissioner of Hexi to hold them back.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃既自恃兵強，每通表疏，求敵國之禮，言詞悖慢，上甚怒之。

translations.literal: Tubo, relying on its military strength, in every memorial and letter sought ritual as between equal states; the wording was arrogant and slow; the emperor was very angry at this.
translations.idiomatic: Confident in its armies, Tubo demanded in its letters the etiquette due an equal power; its language was insolent, and the emperor was deeply angered.

sentences.zh: 及封禪禮畢，中書令張說奏言：「吐蕃醜逆，誠負萬誅，然又事征討，實為勞弊。

translations.literal: When the Fengshan rites were completed, Chief Minister Zhang Yue memorialized: "Tubo is vile and rebellious and truly deserves ten thousand executions; yet again to undertake punitive campaigns would in fact weary and exhaust us.
translations.idiomatic: After the Fengshan ceremonies, Chief Minister Zhang Yue submitted: "Tubo is wicked and rebellious and deserves death ten thousand times over, yet further campaigns would only exhaust us.

sentences.zh: 且十數年甘、涼、河、鄯征發不息，縱令屬勝，亦不能補。

translations.literal: Moreover for more than ten years Gan, Liang, He, and Shan have known levies and expeditions without cease; even if we should win every battle, we still could not make up the loss.
translations.idiomatic: For more than a decade Gan, Liang, He, and Shan have been mobilized without rest; even victory cannot repay what has been spent.

sentences.zh: 聞其悔過請和，惟陛下遣使。

translations.literal: We hear that they repent and request peace—only that Your Majesty send envoys.
translations.idiomatic: They now repent and sue for peace. I beg that Your Majesty send envoys.

sentences.zh: 許其稽顙內屬，以息邊境，則蒼生幸甚。

translations.literal: Grant that they bow their foreheads and submit inward, to give rest to the borderlands—then the black-haired masses would be greatly fortunate."
translations.idiomatic: Let them knock their foreheads and enter our allegiance, that the frontier may rest—so the people would be greatly blessed."

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「待吾與王君籌之。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Wait until I consult with Wang Junyi."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Let me consult Wang Junyi first."

sentences.zh: 」說出，謂源乾曜曰：「君勇而無謀，常思僥幸，兩國和好，何以為勞？

translations.literal: " When Yue went out he said to Yuan Qianyao: "Junyi is brave but without stratagem, always thinking of lucky chances—what hardship is there in good relations between two states?
translations.idiomatic: When Yue left the hall he told Yuan Qianyao: "Junyi is bold but not shrewd and always gambles on luck. What trouble is peace between two realms?

sentences.zh: 若入陳謀，則吾計不遂矣。

translations.literal: If he enters to offer counsel, then our plan will not succeed."
translations.idiomatic: If he speaks before the throne, our design will fail."

sentences.zh: 」尋而君入朝奏事，遂請率兵深入以討之。

translations.literal: " Before long Junyi entered court to report affairs and then requested to lead troops deep in to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Wang Junyi came to court and asked leave to lead a deep strike into Tubo.

sentences.zh: 十五年正月，君率兵破吐蕃於青海之西，虜其輜重及羊馬而還。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fifteenth year Junyi led troops and defeated Tubo west of Qinghai, captured their baggage train and sheep and horses, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fifteenth year Wang Junyi routed Tubo west of Qinghai, seized their baggage and herds, and returned.

sentences.zh: 先是，吐蕃大將悉諾邏率眾入攻大鬥谷，又移攻甘州，焚燒市裏。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Tubo great general Sinuoluo had led his host to attack Dadou Valley and then shifted to attack Ganzhou, burning the market streets.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Tubo commander Sinuoluo had invaded Dadou Valley and turned to storm Ganzhou, burning the markets.

sentences.zh: 君畏其鋒，不敢出戰。

translations.literal: Junyi feared their edge and did not dare go out to fight.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Junyi, daunted by their strength, would not give battle.

sentences.zh: 會大雪，賊凍死者甚眾，遂取積石軍西路而還。

translations.literal: Heavy snow fell; very many of the enemy froze to death; they then took the Jishi Army western road and returned.
translations.idiomatic: A great blizzard followed; countless Tubo soldiers froze on the march. Sinuoluo withdrew by the Jishi Army western route.

sentences.zh: 君先令人潛入賊境，於其歸路燒草。

translations.literal: Junyi had first sent men secretly into enemy territory to burn the grass along their return route.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Junyi had already sent agents into Tubo to burn the pasture along the enemy's line of retreat.

sentences.zh: 悉諾邏軍還至大非山，將士息甲牧馬，而野草皆盡，馬死過半。

translations.literal: When Sinuoluo's army returned to Mount Dafei, the officers and soldiers rested their armor and pastured horses, but the wild grass was all gone and more than half the horses died.
translations.idiomatic: At Mount Dafei the Tubo troops unsaddled to graze, but the grass was gone and more than half their horses perished.

sentences.zh: 君與秦州都督張景順等率眾襲其後，入至青海之西，時海水冰合，將士並乘冰而渡。

translations.literal: Junyi with Qinzhou Protector-general Zhang Jingshun and others led their host to strike their rear; they entered west of Qinghai; at that time the sea waters froze solid and officers and soldiers all crossed on the ice.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Junyi and Qinzhou Protector Zhang Jingshun fell on their rear and marched west of Qinghai. The lake had frozen over, and the whole army crossed on the ice.

sentences.zh: 會悉諾邏已渡大非川，輜重及疲兵尚在青海之側，君縱兵俘之而還。

translations.literal: It happened that Sinuoluo had already crossed the Dafei River; baggage and weary soldiers were still on the Qinghai shore; Junyi loosed his troops, captured them, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Sinuoluo had already crossed the Dafei River, but his baggage and stragglers were still beside Qinghai. Wang Junyi swept down, took them captive, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 其年九月，吐蕃大將悉諾邏恭祿及燭龍莽布支攻陷瓜州城，執刺史田元獻及王君之父壽，盡取城中軍資及倉糧，仍毀其城而去。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of that year the Tubo great generals Sinuoluo Gonglu and Zhulong Mangbuzhi attacked and took Guazhou city, seized Prefect Tian Yuanxian and Wang Junyi's father Shou, took all military stores and granary grain in the city, and still destroyed the city before departing.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of that year the Tubo generals Sinuoluo Gonglu and Zhulong Mangbuzhi stormed Guazhou, seized Prefect Tian Yuanxian and Wang Junyi's father Shou, stripped the garrison stores and granaries, and razed the city as they left.

sentences.zh: 又進攻玉門軍及常樂縣，縣令賈師順嬰城固守，凡八十日，賊遂引退。

translations.literal: They again advanced to attack Yumen Army and Changle County; Magistrate Jia Shishun defended the walls firmly; in all eighty days; the enemy then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: They pressed on against Yumen Army and Changle County. Magistrate Jia Shishun held the walls for eighty days until the raiders withdrew.

sentences.zh: 俄而王君為回紇余黨所殺，乃命兵部尚書蕭嵩為河西節度使，以建康軍使、左金吾將軍張守珪為瓜州刺史，修築州城，招輯百姓，令其復業。

translations.literal: Before long Wang Junyi was killed by remnant Uyghur partisans; the emperor then appointed Minister of War Xiao Song military commissioner of Hexi, and Jiankang Army commissioner, Left Golden Guard General Zhang Shougui, prefect of Guazhou, to repair the prefectural walls, gather and console the people, and order them to resume their livelihoods.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Wang Junyi was slain by remnant Uyghur factions. The emperor appointed Xiao Song, Minister of War, military commissioner of Hexi, and Zhang Shougui of the Jiankang Army, Left Golden Guard General, prefect of Guazhou, to rebuild the walls, gather the people, and restore their livelihoods.

sentences.zh: 時悉諾邏恭祿威名甚振，蕭嵩乃縱反間於吐蕃，雲其與中國潛通，贊普遂召而誅之。

translations.literal: At that time Xi Nuoluo Gonglu's renown was greatly waxing; Xiao Song then spread counter-intelligence among Tubo, saying he was in secret contact with China; the zanpu thereupon summoned and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: By then Xi Nuoluo Gonglu's fame had grown formidable. Xiao Song sowed discord in Tubo, alleging secret dealings with the Tang; the zanpu recalled him and put him to death.

sentences.zh: 明年秋，吐蕃大將悉末朗復率眾攻瓜州，守珪出兵擊走之。

translations.literal: The next autumn, Tubo's great general Ximo Lang again led troops to attack Guazhou; Shougui led his army out and drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: The following autumn the Tubo commander Ximo Lang marched again on Guazhou. Zhang Shougui took the field and repulsed him.

sentences.zh: 隴右節度使、鄯州都督張忠亮引兵至青海西南渴波谷，與吐蕃接戰，大破之。

translations.literal: Longyou military commissioner and Zongzhou protector Zhang Zhongliang led troops to Kebo Valley southwest of Qinghai, engaged Tubo in battle, and inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhongliang, military commissioner of Longyou and protector of Zongzhou, advanced to Kebo Valley southwest of Qinghai, met the Tubo army, and shattered it.

sentences.zh: 俄而積石、莫門兩軍兵馬總至，與忠亮合勢追討，破其大莫門城，生擒千余人，獲馬一千匹、牦牛五百頭，器仗衣資甚眾，又焚其駱駝橋而還。

translations.literal: Soon the armies of Jishi and Momen both arrived in full; joining forces with Zhongliang they pursued and attacked, broke Great Momen City, captured alive more than a thousand men, took a thousand horses and five hundred yaks, and a great quantity of weapons, gear, and clothing; they also burned the Camel Bridge and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the full strength of the Jishi and Momen armies came up. United with Zhongliang they pressed the pursuit, stormed Great Momen City, took more than a thousand prisoners, seized a thousand horses and five hundred yaks, and booty of arms and supplies in vast quantity, then burned the Camel Bridge and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 八月，蕭嵩又遣副將杜賓客率弩手四千人與吐蕃戰於祁連城下，自辰至暮，散而復合，賊徒大潰，臨陣斬其副將一人。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Xiao Song again sent deputy commander Du Binke leading four thousand crossbowmen to fight Tubo below Qilian Fortress; from the fifth watch to evening they scattered and re-formed; the rebel host broke utterly; one of their deputy commanders was beheaded on the field.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Xiao Song sent his deputy Du Binke with four thousand crossbowmen to meet Tubo below Qilian Fortress. From dawn to dusk the lines broke and re-formed; the enemy collapsed in rout, and one of their deputy generals was slain before the ranks.

sentences.zh: 賊敗，散走投山，哭聲四合。

translations.literal: The rebels defeated, scattered and fled into the hills; cries echoed on every side.
translations.idiomatic: Broken, the enemy fled into the hills in disarray, and wailing rose on every hand.

sentences.zh: 初，上聞吐蕃重來入寇，謂侍臣曰：「吐蕃驕暴。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the emperor heard Tubo had come again in force to raid, he told his attendant ministers: "Tubo is arrogant and brutal.
translations.idiomatic: When word first came that Tubo was invading again in strength, the emperor told his ministers, "Tubo grows arrogant and savage.

sentences.zh: 恃力而來，朕今按地圖。

translations.literal: Relying on brute strength they come; I shall now consult the map.
translations.idiomatic: They trust only in force. I shall spread the map

sentences.zh: 審利害，親指授將帥，破之必矣！

translations.literal: Weigh advantage and harm, personally direct the generals—breaking them is certain!"
translations.idiomatic: and weigh gain and loss, then direct the commanders myself. Their defeat is assured!"

sentences.zh: 」數日而露布至。

translations.literal: Within several days the victory bulletin arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Within days the victory dispatch arrived.

sentences.zh: 十七年，朔方大總管信安王祎又率兵赴隴右，拔其石堡城，斬首四百余級，生擒二百余口，遂於石堡城置振武軍，仍獻其俘囚於太廟。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, Grand Commander of Shuofang Prince Xin'an Wang Yi again led troops to Longyou, took their Stone Fortress, cut off over four hundred heads, captured alive over two hundred persons; he then established Zhenwu Army at Stone Fortress and still presented the captives at the Imperial Ancestors' temple.
