translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year Prince Xin'an Wang Yi, grand commander of Shuofang, marched again into Longyou, seized Stone Fortress, took more than four hundred heads and two hundred prisoners, garrisoned Zhenwu Army there, and presented the captives at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 於是吐蕃頻遣使請和，忠王友皇甫惟明因奏事面陳通和之便。

translations.literal: Then Tubo repeatedly sent envoys requesting peace; Huangfu Weiming, friend of the Prince of Zhong, memorialized on other business and in person set forth the advantages of alliance.
translations.idiomatic: Tubo then sent envoys again and again to sue for peace. Huangfu Weiming, a companion of the Prince of Zhong, came before the throne on other business and argued face to face for reconciliation.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「吐蕃贊普往年嘗與朕書，悖慢無禮，朕意欲討之，何得和也！

translations.literal: The emperor said: "The Tubo zanpu in past years sent me a letter, insolent and without courtesy; I intend to punish them—how can there be peace!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "The Tubo zanpu once wrote to me in terms insolent and rude. I mean to chastise them—how can we speak of peace!"

sentences.zh: 」惟明曰：「開元之初，贊普幼稚，豈能如此。

translations.literal: " Weiming said: "At the start of Kaiyuan the zanpu was still young; he could not have done such a thing.
translations.idiomatic: Weiming replied, "At the opening of the Kaiyuan era the zanpu was still a child. He could not have written so.

sentences.zh: 必是在邊軍將務邀一時之功，偽作此書，激怒陛下。

translations.literal: It must have been frontier generals seeking momentary glory, forging this letter to anger Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: Surely frontier officers, hungry for a quick triumph, forged the letter to stir Your Majesty's wrath.

sentences.zh: 兩國既鬥，興師動眾，因利乘便，公行隱盜，偽作功狀，以希勛爵，所損鉅萬，何益國家！

translations.literal: Once the two states fight, armies are raised; seizing opportunity for profit, theft is openly practiced, false merit reports forged to win honors—losses run to myriads, what benefit to the state!
translations.idiomatic: Once the two realms are at war, armies march and men steal under cover of campaign, inventing battle reports to win honors. The cost runs to tens of thousands—what good does the state gain?

sentences.zh: 今河西、隴右，百姓疲竭，事皆由此。

translations.literal: Now Hexi and Longyou—the people are worn out; all stems from this.
translations.idiomatic: Today the people of Hexi and Longyou are spent to the bone, and all of it comes from this.

sentences.zh: 若陛下遣使往視金城公主，因與贊普面約通和，令其稽顙稱臣，永息邊境，此永代安人之道也。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty sends envoys to visit Princess Jincheng and with the zanpu face to face arranges peace, making him bow and call himself subject, forever quieting the border—this is the way to secure the people for all generations.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty sends envoys to visit Princess Jincheng and there, face to face with the zanpu, binds a lasting peace—making him bow and acknowledge subjection and stilling the frontier forever—that is the way to settle the realm for ages.

sentences.zh: 」上然其言，因令惟明及內侍張元方充使往問吐蕃。

translations.literal: " The emperor approved his words and thereupon ordered Weiming and eunuch Zhang Yuanfang to serve as envoys to Tubo.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor assented and appointed Weiming and the palace eunuch Zhang Yuanfang envoys to Tubo.

sentences.zh: 惟明、元方等至吐蕃，既見贊普及公主，具宣上意。

translations.literal: Weiming, Yuanfang and the others reached Tubo; having seen the zanpu and the princess, they fully proclaimed the emperor's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Weiming and Yuanfang reached Tubo, were received by the zanpu and the princess, and laid out the emperor's will in full.

sentences.zh: 贊普等欣然請和，盡出貞觀以來前後敕書以示惟明等，令其重臣名悉獵隨惟明等入朝，上表曰：

translations.literal: The zanpu and others gladly requested peace, produced all imperial edicts from Zhenguan onward for Weiming and the others to see, and ordered his senior minister Ming Xilie to accompany Weiming and the others to court; they submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: The zanpu and his court gladly sought peace, produced every imperial edict since Zhenguan for Weiming to read, and sent his chief minister Ming Xilie back to Chang'an with the embassy. Their memorial read:

sentences.zh: 外甥是先皇帝舅宿親，又蒙降金城公主，遂和同為一家，天下百姓，普皆安樂。

translations.literal: Your nephew-by-marriage is the Late Emperor's kin by marriage; having also been granted Princess Jincheng, we became one family in harmony; all the people under Heaven everywhere enjoy peace.
translations.idiomatic: Your nephew-by-marriage is the Late Emperor's kin by marriage. Having also been granted Princess Jincheng, we became one household in amity, and all the people under Heaven lived in peace.

sentences.zh: 中間為張玄表、李知古等東西兩處先動兵馬，侵抄吐蕃，邊將所以互相征討，迄至今日，遂成釁隙。

translations.literal: In between, Zhang Xuanbiao, Li Zhigu and others on east and west both first moved troops, raiding Tubo; frontier generals therefore attacked one another back and forth down to today, and thus the breach arose.
translations.idiomatic: Between those days Zhang Xuanbiao, Li Zhigu, and others on east and west were first to move troops and raid Tubo. Frontier commanders have struck back and forth ever since, until today the rift has widened.

sentences.zh: 外甥以先代文成公主、今金城公主之故，深識尊卑，豈敢失禮！

translations.literal: Your nephew, for the sake of the former Princess Wencheng and the present Princess Jincheng, deeply understands superior and inferior—how would I dare breach propriety!
translations.idiomatic: For the sake of Princess Wencheng of old and Princess Jincheng today your nephew knows well the order of superior and inferior. How would I dare breach propriety!

sentences.zh: 又緣年小，枉被邊將讒抅鬥亂，令舅致怪。

translations.literal: Moreover being young, I was wrongly slandered by frontier generals into strife, causing Uncle to take offense.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, being young, I was wrongly slandered by frontier generals into quarrel, and so caused my uncle's displeasure.

sentences.zh: 伏乞垂察追留，死將萬足。

translations.literal: I humbly beg you to investigate and retain me; death would still be insufficient.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly beg you to look into this and keep me in your grace; even death would not repay my debt.

sentences.zh: 前數度使人入朝，皆被邊將不許，所以不敢自奏。

translations.literal: Several times before envoys entered court but were barred by frontier generals, so I did not dare memorialize myself.
translations.idiomatic: Several times before I sent envoys to court, but frontier generals would not let them pass, and so I did not dare petition on my own.

sentences.zh: 去冬公主遣使人婁眾失若將狀專往，蒙降使看公主來，外甥不勝喜荷。

translations.literal: Last winter the princess sent attendant Lou Zhongshiluo with a petition solely for this purpose; we received your gracious dispatch to view the princess on our behalf—your nephew is overcome with grateful joy.
translations.idiomatic: Last winter the princess sent her attendant Lou Zhongshiluo with a petition devoted to this end. We received your gracious order to visit the princess on our behalf. Your nephew is overcome with grateful joy.

sentences.zh: 謹遣諭名悉獵及副使押衙將軍浪些紇夜悉獵入朝，奏取進止。

translations.literal: Respectfully I send Ming Xilie as spokesman and deputy commissioner, guard-general Langxiexie Yexi Lie, and others to court to report and await orders.
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully send Ming Xilie as spokesman, with deputy commissioner and guard-general Langxiexie Yexi Lie, to court to report and await your command.

sentences.zh: 兩國事意，悉獵所知。

translations.literal: The affairs and intent of both states—Ming Xilie knows them.
translations.idiomatic: Ming Xilie knows the mind of both realms in full.

sentences.zh: 外甥蕃中已處分邊將，不許抄掠，若有漢人來投，便令卻送。

translations.literal: Your nephew has already disposed among Tubo that frontier generals may not raid; if Han people come over to us, they are to be sent back.
translations.idiomatic: Your nephew has already ordered Tubo's frontier commanders to cease raiding. Any Han who flee to us are to be returned.

sentences.zh: 伏望皇帝舅遠察赤心，許依舊好，長令百姓快樂。

translations.literal: I hope the August Emperor-uncle will from afar discern this loyal heart and permit the old friendship, ever letting the people be at ease.
translations.idiomatic: I hope the August Emperor-uncle will discern my loyal heart from afar, restore our old friendship, and let the people live in ease forever.

sentences.zh: 如蒙聖恩，千年萬歲，外甥終不敢先違盟誓。

translations.literal: If we receive the sage favor, for a thousand myriad years your nephew will never dare first to break the covenant.
translations.idiomatic: If we receive your sage grace, for a thousand myriad years your nephew will never be first to break the covenant.

sentences.zh: 謹奉金胡瓶一、金盤一、金碗一、馬腦杯一、零羊衫段一，謹充微國之禮。

translations.literal: Respectfully offering one gold Hu vessel, one gold tray, one gold bowl, one agate cup, and one length of lingyang felt and silk robes—as token gifts of our humble state.
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully present one gold Hu flask, one gold tray, one gold bowl, one agate cup, and one length of lingyang felt and silk—as the humble gifts of our state.

sentences.zh: 金城公主又別進金鴨盤盞雜器物等。

translations.literal: Princess Jincheng also separately presented gold duck platters, vessels, and other miscellaneous objects.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Jincheng also sent separately gold duck platters, cups, and other objects.

sentences.zh: 十八年十月，名悉獵等至京師，上御宣政殿，列羽林仗以見之。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the eighteenth year Ming Xilie and the others reached the capital; the emperor received them at Xuanzheng Hall with a guard of Feathered Forest troops arrayed.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the eighteenth year Ming Xilie and his party reached the capital. The emperor received them at Xuanzheng Hall with the Feathered Forest guard drawn up in array.

sentences.zh: 悉獵頗曉書記，先曾迎金城公主至長安，當時朝廷皆稱其才辯。

translations.literal: Xi Lie was quite versed in writing and record; he had earlier welcomed Princess Jincheng to Chang'an; at that time the court all praised his talent in debate.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Lie was skilled in writing and record. He had earlier escorted Princess Jincheng to Chang'an, and the court had then praised his eloquence.

sentences.zh: 及是上引入內宴，與語，甚禮之。

translations.literal: When now the emperor brought him in to an inner banquet and conversed with him, he treated him with great courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: On this occasion the emperor brought him to an inner banquet, spoke with him at length, and honored him greatly.

sentences.zh: 賜紫袍金帶及魚袋，並時服、繒彩、銀盤、胡瓶，仍於別館供擬甚厚。

translations.literal: He granted a purple robe, gold belt, and fish tally, also seasonal garments, silks, silver trays, and Hu vessels; lodgings in a separate hostel were lavishly supplied.
translations.idiomatic: He was given a purple robe, gold belt, and fish tally, together with court dress, silks, silver trays, and Hu flasks, and lodged in a separate hostel with lavish provision.

sentences.zh: 悉獵受袍帶器物而卻進魚袋，辭曰：「本國無此章服，不敢當殊異之賞。

translations.literal: Xi Lie accepted the robe, belt, and vessels but returned the fish tally, declining: "Our state has no such insignia of rank—we dare not accept extraordinary reward."
translations.idiomatic: Xi Lie accepted the robe, belt, and vessels but returned the fish tally, saying, "Our realm has no such insignia of rank. I dare not accept so extraordinary a gift."

sentences.zh: 」上嘉而許之。

translations.literal: " The emperor praised this and permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised his modesty and agreed.

sentences.zh: 詔御史大夫崔琳充使報聘。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Censor-in-chief Cui Lin to serve as return envoy.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed Censor-in-chief Cui Lin return envoy.

sentences.zh: 仍於赤嶺各豎分界之碑，約以更不相侵。

translations.literal: Boundary markers were likewise erected at Chiling on each side, with a covenant that neither would again invade the other.
translations.idiomatic: At Chiling each side also raised boundary steles, covenanting that neither would invade the other again.

sentences.zh: 時吐蕃使奏云：「公主請《毛詩》、《禮記》、《左傳》《文選》各一部。

translations.literal: At that time a Tubo envoy memorialized: "The princess requests one copy each of the Mao Odes, the Book of Rites, the Zuo Tradition to the Spring and Autumn Annals, and the Literary Anthology."
translations.idiomatic: A Tubo envoy then reported, "The princess requests one copy each of the Mao Odes, the Book of Rites, the Zuo Tradition, and the Literary Anthology."

sentences.zh: 」制令秘書省寫與之。

translations.literal: " An order directed the Secretariat to copy and give them.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial order directed the Secretariat to copy and furnish them.

sentences.zh: 正字於休烈上疏請曰：

translations.literal: Principal Archivist Yu Xiulie submitted a memorial petition, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Principal Archivist Yu Xiulie submitted a memorial, saying:

sentences.zh: 臣聞戎狄，國之寇也；

translations.literal: I have heard that the Rong and Di are the state's enemies;
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that the Rong and Di are the state's enemies;

sentences.zh: 經籍，國之典也。

translations.literal: the classics are the state's canon.
translations.idiomatic: the classics are the state's canon.

sentences.zh: 戎之生心，不可以無備；

translations.literal: When the Rong harbor designs, we may not be without defense;
translations.idiomatic: When the Rong harbor designs, we may not be without defense;

sentences.zh: 典有恆制，不可以假人。

translations.literal: canonical norms have constant regulation—they may not be lent to others.
translations.idiomatic: canonical norms have fixed rule—they may not be lent to others.

sentences.zh: 《傳》曰：「裔不謀夏，夷不亂華。

translations.literal: The Tradition says: "Descendants do not plot against Xia; barbarians do not disorder the Chinese."
translations.idiomatic: The Tradition says, "Descendants do not plot against Xia; barbarians do not disorder the Chinese."

sentences.zh: 」所以格其非心，在乎有備無患。

translations.literal: " Thus to curb their disloyal hearts lies in being prepared without worry.
translations.idiomatic: Thus to curb their disloyal hearts lies in preparedness without lapse.

sentences.zh: 昔東平王入朝求《史記》、諸子，漢帝不與。

translations.literal: Formerly the Prince of Dongping entered court requesting the Records of the Grand Historian and the Masters; the Han emperor did not grant them.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly the Prince of Dongping came to court requesting the Records of the Grand Historian and the Masters; the Han emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 蓋以《史記》多兵謀，諸子雜詭術。

translations.literal: For the Records are full of military stratagems, and the Masters full of heterodox arts.
translations.idiomatic: For the Records are full of military stratagems, and the Masters full of heterodox arts.

sentences.zh: 夫以東平，漢之懿戚，尚不欲示征戰之書，今西戎，國之寇讎，豈可貽經典之事！

translations.literal: Though Dongping was Han's honored kin, it still would not show books of campaigning—how now Western Rong, the state's foes, may we bestow canonical affairs!
translations.idiomatic: Though Dongping was Han's honored kin, the throne would not show him books of war. How now may we bestow the canon upon Western Rong, the state's sworn foe!

sentences.zh: 且臣聞吐蕃之性，剽悍果決，敏情持銳，善學不回。

translations.literal: Moreover I hear Tubo's nature is fierce and resolute, quick of mind and sharp in grasp, apt at learning and unyielding.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover I hear that Tubo's nature is fierce and resolute, keen of mind and sharp in grasp, apt at learning and unyielding.

sentences.zh: 若達於書，必能知戰。

translations.literal: If they master books they will certainly master war.
translations.idiomatic: If they master books, they will certainly master war.

sentences.zh: 深於《詩》，則知武夫有師幹之試；

translations.literal: Deep in the Odes, they will know that warriors undergo trials of command;
translations.idiomatic: Deep in the Odes, they will learn how warriors are tried in command;

sentences.zh: 深於《禮》，則知月令有興廢之兵；

translations.literal: deep in the Rites, they will know that monthly ordinances hold times for raising and standing down arms;
translations.idiomatic: deep in the Rites, they will learn the monthly ordinances for raising and standing down arms;

sentences.zh: 深於《傳》，則知用師多詭詐之計；

translations.literal: deep in the Tradition, they will know that employing troops employs many stratagems of deceit;
translations.idiomatic: deep in the Tradition, they will learn the stratagems of deceit in employing troops;

sentences.zh: 深於《文》，則知往來有書檄之制。

translations.literal: deep in the Letters, they will know that dealings between states have forms of written proclamation.
translations.idiomatic: deep in the Letters, they will learn the forms of written proclamation between states.

sentences.zh: 何異借寇兵而資盜糧也！

translations.literal: What difference from lending enemy troops and provisioning bandit grain!
translations.idiomatic: What is this but lending arms to the foe and grain to the bandit!

sentences.zh: 臣聞魯秉周禮，齊不加兵；

translations.literal: I have heard that Lu maintained Zhou ritual and Qi did not add troops;
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that Lu upheld Zhou ritual and Qi did not raise arms against it;

sentences.zh: 吳獲乘車，楚疲奔命。

translations.literal: Wu obtained carriage and Chu was worn out racing to answer.
translations.idiomatic: Wu obtained carriage and Chu was worn out racing to answer.

sentences.zh: 一以守典存國，一以喪法危邦，可取鑒也。

translations.literal: One preserved the canon and saved the state; one abandoned law and endangered the realm—a lesson to be taken.
translations.idiomatic: One preserved the canon and saved the state; one abandoned law and endangered the realm. Here is a lesson.

sentences.zh: 且公主下嫁從人，遠適異國，合慕夷禮，返求良書，愚臣料之，恐非公主本意也。

translations.literal: Moreover the princess going down to marry with her retinue, traveling far to an alien land—she ought to admire barbarian ritual, not turn back to seek fine books; this humble official reckons that I fear this is not the princess's true intent.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the princess went down in marriage with her retinue to a distant alien land. She ought to admire barbarian custom, not turn back to seek fine books. This humble official reckons this is not the princess's true intent.

sentences.zh: 慮有奔北之類，勸教於中。

translations.literal: I worry there are defectors of the north type counseling teaching within.
translations.idiomatic: I fear there are men of the north who have fled and now counsel such teaching within.

sentences.zh: 若陛下慮失蕃情，以備國信，必不得已，請去《春秋》。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty fears losing Tubo favor to preserve state trust and absolutely must, please omit the Spring and Autumn Annals.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty fears losing Tubo's goodwill to preserve state trust and absolutely must grant the books, I beg that at least the Spring and Autumn Annals be withheld.

sentences.zh: 當周德既衰，諸侯強盛，禮樂自出，戰伐交興，情偽於是乎生，變詐於是乎起，則有以臣召君之事，取威定霸之名。

translations.literal: When Zhou virtue had declined, the feudal lords grew strong, ritual and music issued from themselves, campaigning and warfare rose together—sincerity and falsehood then arose, shifts and fraud then sprouted; then there were matters of subjects summoning lords, names of taking power and fixing hegemony.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou virtue had waned, the feudal lords grew strong, ritual and music issued from themselves, and war rose in turn. Sincerity and falsehood were born; shift and fraud sprouted. Then came subjects summoning their lords and names of seizing power and fixing hegemony.

sentences.zh: 若與此書，國之患也。

translations.literal: To give them this book would be the state's calamity.
translations.idiomatic: To give them this book would be calamity for the state.

sentences.zh: 《傳》曰：「於奚請曲縣鞶纓，仲尼曰：『惜也，不如多與之邑。

translations.literal: The Tradition says: "Xi of the Rong requested the music of the Bend in the Huang and the tassels of investiture; Confucius said: 'A pity—better to give him more towns.'"
translations.idiomatic: The Tradition says, "Xi of the Rong requested the music of the Bend in the Huang and the tassels of investiture. Confucius said, 'A pity—it were better to give him more towns.'"

sentences.zh: 惟名與器，不可假人。

translations.literal: "Titles and regalia may not be lent to others."
translations.idiomatic: "Titles and regalia may not be lent to others."

sentences.zh: 』」狄固貪婪，貴貨易土，正可錫之錦綺，厚以玉帛，何必率從其求，以資其智！

translations.literal: "The Di are by nature greedy, valuing goods and trading land—one may bestow silks and brocades, heap jade and silks—why must we follow all their requests and supply their wits!"
translations.idiomatic: The Di are greedy by nature, prizing goods and trading land. Bestow silks and brocades, heap jade and silks upon them—why follow every request and feed their wits!

sentences.zh: 臣忝叨列位，職刊秘籍，實痛經典，棄在戎夷。

translations.literal: Your servant has the misfortune to stand in the ranks, charged with editing secret archives—I truly grieve that the classics should be cast among the Rong and Di.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant stands unworthily in the ranks, charged with editing the secret archives. I grieve in truth to see the classics cast among the Rong and Di.

sentences.zh: 昧死上聞，惟陛下深察。

translations.literal: Braving death I report upward; may Your Majesty deeply consider.
translations.idiomatic: Braving death I report this upward. May Your Majesty consider it deeply.

sentences.zh: 疏奏不省。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted and not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was submitted and ignored.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，又制工部尚書李皓往聘吐蕃。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year, an order again appointed Minister of Works Li Hao to go on a friendly mission to Tubo.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year an order again appointed Li Hao, Minister of Works, envoy to Tubo.

sentences.zh: 每唐使入境，所在盛陳甲兵及騎馬，以矜其精銳。

translations.literal: Whenever Tang envoys entered their border, everywhere armor and cavalry were displayed in strength to show off their elite.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Tang envoys crossed the border, armor and cavalry were massed everywhere to display their strength.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，遣將軍李佺於赤嶺與吐蕃分界立碑。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year, General Li Quan was sent to Chiling to set up boundary markers with Tubo.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year General Li Quan was sent to Chiling to erect boundary steles with Tubo.

sentences.zh: 二十四年正月，吐蕃遣使貢方物金銀器玩數百事，皆形制奇異。

translations.literal: In the first month of the twenty-fourth year Tubo sent envoys presenting tribute of local products—over a hundred gold and silver vessels and curios, all strange in form.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the twenty-fourth year Tubo sent envoys with tribute of more than a hundred gold and silver vessels and curios, all strange in form.

sentences.zh: 上令列於提象門外，以示百僚。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered them displayed outside the Gate of the Raised Elephant for the hundred officials to see.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered them set out before the Gate of the Raised Elephant for the hundred officials to view.

sentences.zh: 其年，吐蕃西擊勃律，遣使來告急。

translations.literal: That year Tubo attacked Bolor in the west and sent envoys to report emergency.
translations.idiomatic: That year Tubo struck Bolor in the west and sent envoys begging urgent aid.

sentences.zh: 上使報吐蕃，令其罷兵。

translations.literal: The emperor sent word to Tubo ordering them to cease troops.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent word to Tubo ordering them to stand down.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃不受詔，遂攻破勃律國，上甚怒之。

translations.literal: Tubo did not accept the edict and thereupon broke and took the state of Bolor; the emperor was greatly angered.
translations.idiomatic: Tubo refused the edict, overran the state of Bolor, and the emperor was deeply angered.

sentences.zh: 時散騎常侍崔希逸為河西節度使，於涼州鎮守。

translations.literal: At that time Palace Attendant Cui Xiyi was military commissioner of Hexi, garrisoning at Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Cui Xiyi, Palace Attendant, was military commissioner of Hexi, holding Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 時吐蕃與漢樹柵為界，置守捉使。

translations.literal: Then Tubo and Han set palisades as boundary and posted frontier guard commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: Tubo and the Han each had palisades for a boundary and posted frontier guard commissioners.

sentences.zh: 希逸謂吐蕃將乞力徐曰：「兩國和好，何須守捉，妨人耕種。

translations.literal: Xiyi said to the Tubo general Qili Xu: "The two states are friendly—why need frontier guards, harming people's planting?
translations.idiomatic: Xiyi said to the Tubo general Qili Xu, "The two realms are at peace. Why keep frontier guards and hinder the farmers?

sentences.zh: 請皆罷之，以成一家豈不善也？

translations.literal: Please abolish them all—would it not be fine to complete one family?"
translations.idiomatic: Let us abolish them all and complete one household. Would that not be well?"

sentences.zh: 」乞力徐報曰：「常侍忠厚，必是誠言。

translations.literal: " Qili Xu replied: "The regular attendant is honest and generous—surely these are sincere words.
translations.idiomatic: Qili Xu replied, "The regular attendant is honest and generous. These must be sincere words.

sentences.zh: 但恐朝廷未必皆相信任。

translations.literal: But I fear the court may not all believe and trust.
translations.idiomatic: But I fear the court may not all believe and trust.

sentences.zh: 萬一有人交抅，掩吾不備，後悔無益也。

translations.literal: If perchance someone sows discord and strikes when we are unprepared, regret would be of no use."
translations.idiomatic: If someone should sow discord and strike when we are unprepared, regret would come too late."

sentences.zh: 」希逸固請之，遂發使與乞力徐殺白狗為盟，各去守備。

translations.literal: " Xiyi pressed insistently; they then sent envoys with Qili Xu to kill a white dog as oath and each removed their guards.
translations.idiomatic: Xiyi pressed him hard. They then sent envoys, and he and Qili Xu slew a white dog in covenant and each withdrew their guards.

sentences.zh: 於是吐蕃畜牧被野。

translations.literal: Then Tubo's herds grazed across the wild.
translations.idiomatic: Tubo's herds then grazed across the open country.

sentences.zh: 俄而希逸傔人孫誨入朝奏事，誨欲自邀其功，因奏言「吐蕃無備，若發兵掩之，必克捷。

translations.literal: Soon Xiyi's retainer Sun Hui entered court to memorialize; Hui wished to claim merit for himself and therefore reported: "Tubo is without defenses—if we raise troops and strike by surprise, victory is certain."
translations.idiomatic: Before long Xiyi's retainer Sun Hui came to court on business. Wishing to claim merit for himself, he reported, "Tubo is undefended. If we raise troops and strike by surprise, victory is certain."

sentences.zh: 」上使內給事趙惠琮與孫誨馳往觀察事宜。

translations.literal: " The emperor sent Inner Attendant-in-Ordinary Zhao Huizong with Sun Hui riding post-haste to observe affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Inner Attendant-in-Ordinary Zhao Huizong with Sun Hui post-haste to observe the situation.

sentences.zh: 惠琮等至涼州，遂矯詔令希逸掩襲之，希逸不得已而從之，大破吐蕃於青海之上，殺獲甚眾，乞力徐輕身遁逸。

translations.literal: Huizong and the others reached Liangzhou and forged an edict ordering Xiyi to strike by surprise; Xiyi had no choice but to obey; they routed Tubo greatly above Qinghai, killing and capturing in great numbers; Qili Xu fled light-bodied.
translations.idiomatic: Huizong and his party reached Liangzhou and forged an edict ordering Xiyi to strike by surprise. Xiyi had no choice but to obey. They routed Tubo greatly on the Qinghai shore, killing and capturing in vast numbers, while Qili Xu fled for his life.

sentences.zh: 惠琮、孫誨皆加厚賞，吐蕃自是復絕朝貢。

translations.literal: Huizong and Sun Hui both received enriched rewards; Tubo from this again cut off court tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Huizong and Sun Hui both received lavish rewards. Tubo from that day again cut off court tribute.

sentences.zh: 希逸以失信怏怏，在軍不得誌。

translations.literal: Xiyi, having broken faith, was resentful and ill at ease; in the army he could not fulfill his intent.
translations.idiomatic: Xiyi, having broken faith, brooded in resentment and could not find peace in command.

sentences.zh: 俄遷為河南尹，行至京師，與趙惠琮俱見白狗為祟，相次而死。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to be Henan Intendant; reaching the capital on the road, he and Zhao Huizong both saw a white dog haunting them and died in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was transferred to Henan Intendant. On the road to the capital he and Zhao Huizong both saw a white dog haunting them and died in succession.

sentences.zh: 孫誨亦以罪被戮。

translations.literal: Sun Hui also was executed for crime.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Hui was also executed for his crime.

sentences.zh: 詔以岐州刺史蕭炅為戶部侍郎判涼州事，代希逸為河西節度使；

translations.literal: An edict appointed Xiao Jiong, prefect of Qi Prefecture, Vice Minister of Revenue with charge of Liangzhou affairs, replacing Xi Yi as Hexi military commissioner;
translations.idiomatic: The throne ordered Xiao Jiong, prefect of Qi, to serve as Vice Minister of Revenue and act for Liangzhou, succeeding Xi Yi as commissioner of the Hexi frontier;

sentences.zh: 鄯州都督杜希望為隴右節度使；

translations.literal: Du Xiwang, protector-general of Shan Prefecture, [was made] Longyou military commissioner;
translations.idiomatic: Du Xiwang, protector-general of Shan, was made military commissioner of Longyou;

sentences.zh: 太仆卿王昊為益州長史、劍南節度使，分道經略，以討吐蕃。

translations.literal: Wang Hao, Grand Master of Studs, [was made] chief administrator of Yi Prefecture and Jiannan military commissioner; by separate routes they conducted frontier strategy to attack Tubo.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hao, Grand Master of the Studs, became chief administrator of Yi and commissioner of Jiannan; they were to advance by separate routes and carry the war against Tubo.

sentences.zh: 仍令毀其分界之碑。

translations.literal: They were also ordered to destroy the boundary-marker stele.
translations.idiomatic: The court also ordered the destruction of the border treaty stele.

sentences.zh: 二十六年四月，杜希望率眾攻吐蕃新城，拔之。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the twenty-sixth year, Du Xiwang led troops to attack Tubo's Xincheng and took it.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of year twenty-six of the Kaiyuan era, Du Xiwang stormed Tubo's New City and captured it.

sentences.zh: 以其城為威武軍，發兵一千以鎮之。

translations.literal: That city was made Weiwu Army, and a thousand troops were sent to garrison it.
translations.idiomatic: The place was organized as the Weiwu garrison, with a thousand men stationed there.

sentences.zh: 其年七月，希望又從鄯州發兵奪吐蕃河橋，於河左築鹽泉城。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of that year, Xiwang again raised troops from Shan Prefecture, seized Tubo's river bridge, and built Yancheng on the left bank of the river.
translations.idiomatic: That seventh month Xiwang marched again from Shan, seized the Tubo bridge on the river, and built Salt Spring City on the left bank.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃將兵三萬人以拒官軍，希望引眾擊破之，因於鹽泉城置鎮西軍。

translations.literal: Tubo sent thirty thousand men to resist the government army; Xiwang led his forces, defeated them, and thereby established Zhenxi Army at Yancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Tubo sent thirty thousand men against the imperial army; Xiwang routed them and established the Zhenxi garrison at Salt Spring City.

sentences.zh: 時王昊又率劍南兵募攻其安戎城。

translations.literal: At that time Wang Hao also led Jiannan levy troops to attack their Anrong City.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Wang Hao led Jiannan recruits against Anrong City.

sentences.zh: 先於安戎城左右築兩城，以為攻拒之所，頓兵於蓬婆嶺下，運劍南道資糧以守之。

translations.literal: First he built two cities to the left and right of Anrong City as places for attack and defense, encamped troops below Mount Pengpo, and transported Jiannan circuit grain supplies to hold them.
translations.idiomatic: He first threw up twin fortresses flanking Anrong as bases for the siege, camped under Mount Pengpo, and hauled supplies up the Jiannan road to sustain the force.

sentences.zh: 其年九月，吐蕃悉銳以救安戎城，官軍大敗，兩城並為賊所陷，昊脫身走免，將士已下數萬人及軍糧資仗等並沒於賊。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of that year, Tubo committed all its elite to relieve Anrong; the government army suffered a great defeat; both cities together fell to the rebels; Hao escaped by flight; officers and soldiers numbering tens of thousands, with grain, equipment, and arms, were all lost to the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: That ninth month Tubo hurled its best troops to save Anrong. The imperial army was shattered; both satellite forts fell; Hao alone fled free. Tens of thousands of officers and men, with provisions, stores, and weapons, were swallowed by the enemy.

sentences.zh: 昊坐左遷括州刺史。

translations.literal: Hao, on account of the affair, was demoted and transferred to be prefect of Kuo.
translations.idiomatic: Hao was demoted to prefect of Kuo for his failure.

sentences.zh: 初，昊之在軍，謬賞其子錢帛萬計，並擅與紫袍等，所費鉅萬，坐是尋又重貶為端州高要尉而死。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Hao was in the army, he wrongly rewarded his son money and silk to the count of tens of thousands, and on his own authority bestowed purple robes and the like; the cost was enormous; on this account he was soon again heavily demoted to vice-magistrate of Gaoyao in Duan Prefecture, and died there.
translations.idiomatic: While still in command he had lavished on his son rewards in cash and silk beyond count and had presumptuously given him purple robes and such luxuries at a cost of myriads; for this he was soon demoted again to registrar of Gaoyao in Duan, where he died.

sentences.zh: 二十七年七月，吐蕃又寇白草、安人等軍，敕臨洮、朔方等軍分兵救援。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the twenty-seventh year, Tubo again raided the armies at Baicao, Anren, and elsewhere; an edict ordered Lin-tao, Shuofang, and other commands to divide forces for relief.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of year twenty-seven Tubo struck again at Baicao and Anren garrisons; the throne ordered Lin-tao, Shuofang, and other circuits to send relief in separate columns.

sentences.zh: 時吐蕃於中路屯兵，斷臨洮軍之路。

translations.literal: At that time Tubo encamped troops on the middle route and cut the Lin-tao army's road.
translations.idiomatic: Tubo had planted troops on the main route and severed the Lin-tao garrison's supply line.

sentences.zh: 白水軍守捉使高柬於拒守連旬，俄而賊退，蕭炅遣偏將掩其後，擊破之。

translations.literal: Gao Jian of the Baishui army garrison, in holding out on defense for successive ten-day periods, before long the rebels withdrew; Xiao Jiong dispatched a junior general to take them in the rear and defeat them.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Jian, commander of the Baishui outpost, held them at bay for weeks until the enemy withdrew; then Xiao Jiong sent a flank force to fall on their rear and rout them.

sentences.zh: 王昊既敗之後，詔以華州刺史張宥為益州長史、劍南防禦使，主客員外郎章仇兼瓊為益州司馬、防禦副使。

translations.literal: After Wang Hao's defeat, an edict appointed Zhang You, prefect of Hua, chief administrator of Yi and Jiannan defense commissioner; Zhangqiu Jianqiong, clerk in the Office of the Principal Host, Yi Prefecture marshal and defense vice-commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: After Wang Hao's disaster, Zhang You of Hua was made chief administrator of Yi and Jiannan defense commissioner, with Zhangqiu Jianqiong, outer-office secretary in the host ministry, as his marshal and second-in-command.

sentences.zh: 宥既文吏，素無攻戰之策，兼瓊遂專其戎事。

translations.literal: You being a civil official, had long lacked campaigning strategy; Jianqiong thereupon monopolized military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang You was a civilian with no taste for war; Jianqiong took the field command into his own hands.

sentences.zh: 俄而兼瓊入奏，盛陳攻取安戎之策。

translations.literal: Before long Jianqiong entered court and memorialized, fully setting forth a plan to attack and take Anrong.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Jianqiong went to court and laid out a detailed plan to seize Anrong.

sentences.zh: 上甚悅，徙張宥為光祿卿，拔兼瓊令知益州長史事，代張宥節度，仍為之親畫取城之計。

translations.literal: The sovereign was greatly pleased; Zhang You was moved to be Chamberlain for Ceremonials; Jianqiong was promoted and ordered to act in the chief administrator affairs of Yi, replacing Zhang You as commissioner, and the emperor personally drew for him the plan to take the city.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted. Zhang You was shifted to Chamberlain of the Imperial Clan; Jianqiong was promoted to govern Yi and replaced Zhang as commissioner, while the emperor himself sketched out the scheme for taking the city.

sentences.zh: 二十八年春，兼瓊密與安戎城中吐蕃翟都局及維州別駕董承宴等通謀。

translations.literal: In the spring of the twenty-eighth year, Jianqiong secretly communicated in conspiracy with Zhai Duju of Tubo inside Anrong City and Dong Chengyan, vice-prefect of Wei Prefecture, and others.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of year twenty-eight Jianqiong opened secret contact with the Tubo officer Zhai Duju inside Anrong and Dong Chengyan, vice-prefect of Wei, among others.

sentences.zh: 都局等遂翻城歸款，因引官軍入城，盡殺吐蕃將士，使監察御史許遠率兵鎮守。

translations.literal: Duju and the rest thereupon turned the city in submission; they thereupon led the government army into the city, killed all Tubo officers and soldiers, and had Investigative Censor Xu Yuan lead troops to garrison and hold it.
translations.idiomatic: Duju and his party defected, admitted the imperial troops, and slaughtered every Tubo soldier in the place; Investigative Censor Xu Yuan was left to hold the city.

sentences.zh: 上聞之，甚悅。

translations.literal: The sovereign heard it and was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the throne, the emperor was overjoyed.

sentences.zh: 中書令李林甫等上表曰：「伏以吐蕃此城，正當沖要，憑險自固，恃以窺邊。

translations.literal: Chief Minister Li Linfu and others submitted a memorial saying: "We prostrate ourselves: this Tubo city lies right in a strategic chokepoint; relying on its rugged terrain it fortifies itself and presumes to spy upon the border.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Li Linfu and his colleagues memorialized: "This Tubo stronghold sits on a vital pass; trusting its cliffs, it has fortified itself and eyed our frontier.

sentences.zh: 積年以來，蟻聚為患，縱有百萬之眾，難以施功。

translations.literal: For accumulated years it has gathered like ants and become a calamity; even with a force of a million it would be hard to apply military effort.
translations.idiomatic: Years of raids have swarmed like ants upon us; even a million men could not easily take it.

sentences.zh: 陛下親紆秘策，不興師旅，頃令中使李思敬曉喻羌族，莫不懷恩，翻然改圖，自相謀陷。

translations.literal: Your Majesty personally bent your secret stratagem; without raising armies and brigades, you recently had palace emissary Li Sijing explain and instruct the Qiang tribes; none failed to cherish grace; they suddenly changed their design and conspired against one another to ensnare [the foe].
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty devised the secret plan yourself—no great host was needed. The palace agent Li Sijing won over the Qiang, who turned in gratitude and plotted among themselves to betray the garrison.

sentences.zh: 神算運於不測，睿略通於未然，累載逋誅，一朝蕩滅。

translations.literal: Divine calculation operated in what could not be fathomed; sagely design penetrated what had not yet come to be; years of escaped execution were in one morning swept away.
translations.idiomatic: Your foresight worked where none could guess it; your design reached into a future none yet saw—and a foe that had defied us for years was swept away in a single morning.

sentences.zh: 又臣等今日奏事，陛下從容問臣等曰：『卿等但看四夷不久當漸摧喪。

translations.literal: Moreover when we ministers today presented matters at court, Your Majesty at leisure asked us ministers: 'You ministers need only watch—the Four Barbarians before long shall gradually be broken and ruined.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier today, as we reported to you, Your Majesty said with easy calm: "Mark my words—the four quarters of barbarians will soon crack and fail.

sentences.zh: 』德音才降，遽聞戎捷，則知聖與天合，應如響至，前古以來，所未有也。

translations.literal: Your virtuous pronouncement had scarcely descended when we hastily heard news of frontier victory; then we know the sacred is in accord with Heaven, responding like an echo arriving; from antiquity until now, there has never been such a thing.
translations.idiomatic: Your prophecy had barely been uttered when tidings of victory arrived—proof that your sage will moves with Heaven's, that the world answers you like an echo. Never in antiquity was such a thing heard of.

sentences.zh: 請宣示百僚，編諸史策。

translations.literal: We request that it be proclaimed to the hundred officials and entered in the historical annals.
translations.idiomatic: We beg that this be proclaimed to the court and recorded in the histories.

sentences.zh: 」手制答曰：「此城儀鳳年中羌引吐蕃，遂被固守，歲月既久，攻伐亦多。

translations.literal: The emperor's own rescript replied: "This city—in the Yifeng years the Qiang drew in Tubo, and it was thereupon firmly held; months and years have been long; attacks and punitive expeditions have also been many.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor answered in his own hand: "In the Yifeng era the Qiang brought Tubo into this place, which they have held ever since. Long years of assault have failed to move it.

sentences.zh: 其地險阻，非力所制。

translations.literal: Its terrain is perilous and obstructed; it is not what force can control.
translations.idiomatic: The ground is too rugged for force alone to master.

sentences.zh: 朝廷群議，不合取之。

translations.literal: The court's collective deliberation was that it was not fitting to take it.
translations.idiomatic: The court had agreed not to pursue it.

sentences.zh: 朕以小蕃無知，事須處置，授以奇計，所以行之，獲彼戎心，歸我城守，有足為慰也。

translations.literal: We regard this petty barbarian land as ignorant; the matter required disposition; We conferred a wondrous stratagem, and on that account carried it out; We obtained their martial hearts and returned our city garrison—this is sufficient for comfort.
translations.idiomatic: These small barbarians act without counsel; the matter required handling. I gave them a subtle plan, and it succeeded: their hearts came over to us and the city returned to our hold. That is comfort enough.

sentences.zh: 」其年十月，吐蕃又引眾寇安戎城及維州，章仇兼瓊遣裨將率眾禦之，仍發關中彍騎以救援焉。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of that year, Tubo again led masses to raid Anrong City and Wei Prefecture; Zhangqiu Jianqiong sent lieutenant generals leading troops to resist them, and also sent out Guanzhong crossbow-cavalry to rescue there.
translations.idiomatic: That tenth month Tubo struck again at Anrong and Wei. Jianqiong sent subordinate generals to meet them and mobilized Guanzhong mounted archers as reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 時屬凝寒，賊久之自引退。

translations.literal: The season was severe cold; the rebels after long time withdrew of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: The bitter cold finally drove them off.

sentences.zh: 詔改安戎城為平戎城。

translations.literal: An edict changed Anrong City to Pingrong City.
translations.idiomatic: The court renamed Anrong "Pacify-the-Barbarians City."

sentences.zh: 二十九年春，金城公主薨，吐蕃遣使來告哀，仍請和，上不許之。

translations.literal: In the spring of the twenty-ninth year, Princess Jincheng died; Tubo sent envoys to announce mourning and also sought peace; the sovereign did not grant it.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of year twenty-nine Princess Jincheng died. Tubo sent envoys to announce the loss and sue for peace; the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 使到數月後，始為公主舉哀於光順門外，輟朝三日。

translations.literal: After the envoys arrived several months later, mourning for the princess was first performed outside Guangshun Gate; court was halted three days.
translations.idiomatic: Only months after the envoys arrived did the court hold mourning for the princess outside Guangshun Gate and suspend audience for three days.

sentences.zh: 六月，吐蕃四十萬攻承風堡，至河源軍，西入長寧橋，至安仁軍，渾崖峰騎將盛希液以眾五千攻而破之。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, four hundred thousand Tubo attacked Chengfeng Fortress, reached Heyuan Army, entered west at Changning Bridge, reached Anren Army; Sheng Xiye, cavalry general of Hunyafeng, with five thousand men attacked and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month four hundred thousand Tubo struck Chengfeng Fortress, advanced to Heyuan Army, crossed west by Changning Bridge toward Anren Army—and Sheng Xiye of the Hunyafeng cavalry, with five thousand men, attacked and broke them.

sentences.zh: 十二月，吐蕃又襲石堡城，節度使蓋嘉運不能守，玄宗憤之。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Tubo again raided Stone Fortress City; Military Commissioner Gai Jiayun could not hold it; Xuanzong was enraged at this.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Tubo raided Stone Fortress again. Commissioner Gai Jiayun could not hold it, and Xuanzong fumed.

sentences.zh: 天寶初，令皇甫惟明、王忠嗣為隴右節度，皆不能克。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao, Huangfu Weiming and Wang Zhongsi were made Longyou commissioners; both could not capture it.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianbao era Huangfu Weiming and Wang Zhongsi were sent as Longyou commissioners; neither could take the place.

sentences.zh: 七載，以哥舒翰為隴右節度使，攻而拔之，改石堡城為神武軍。

translations.literal: In the seventh year [of Tianbao], Ge Shuhan was made Longyou military commissioner; he attacked and captured it; Stone Fortress City was changed to Shenwu Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Tianbao Ge Shuhan became Longyou commissioner, stormed and took the fortress, and renamed it the Shenwu garrison.

sentences.zh: 天寶十四載，贊普乞黎蘇籠獵贊死，大臣立其子婆悉籠獵贊為主，復為贊普。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Tianbao, the zanpu Qili Sulungliezan died; great ministers installed his son Bosuolongliezan as lord and again made him zanpu.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianbao fourteen the zanpu Qili Sulungliezan died. His ministers raised his son Bosuolongliezan to the throne as zanpu once more.

sentences.zh: 玄宗遣京兆少尹崔光遠兼御史中丞，持節賫國信冊命吊祭之。

translations.literal: Xuanzong sent Capital Assistant Intendant Cui Guangyuan, concurrently Censor-in-Chief, bearing the staff of office to convey the imperial letter of credence, patent of appointment, and condolences for the rites of mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong dispatched Cui Guangyuan, assistant intendant of the capital and censor-in-chief, with imperial credentials to invest the new ruler and perform the mourning rites.

sentences.zh: 及還，而安祿山已竊據洛陽，以河、隴兵募令哥舒翰為將，屯潼關。

translations.literal: When he returned, An Lushan had already seized Luoyang in stealth; with He-Long levy troops Ge Shuhan was made general and encamped at Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he found that An Lushan had seized Luoyang; Ge Shuhan was appointed to command the He-Long levies and hold Tong Pass.

sentences.zh: 昔秦以隴山已西為隴西郡。

translations.literal: Formerly Qin made the region west of Long Mountains Longxi Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In Qin times the land west of the Long Mountains formed Longxi Commandery.

sentences.zh: 漢懷匈奴於河右，置姑臧、張掖、酒泉、伊吾等郡；

translations.literal: Han pacified the Xiongnu on the river's right, establishing Guzang, Zhangye, Jiuquan, Yiwu, and other commanderies;
translations.idiomatic: Han wooed the Xiongnu west of the river and founded the commanderies of Guzang, Zhangye, Jiuquan, Yiwu, and the rest;

sentences.zh: 又於磧外置西域都護，控引胡國；

translations.literal: Further, beyond the desert they placed the Protectorate of the Western Regions, controlling and drawing in barbarian states;
translations.idiomatic: beyond the sands they set the Western Regions protectorate to oversee the barbarian kingdoms;

sentences.zh: 又分隴西為金城、西平等郡，雜以氐、羌居之。

translations.literal: Further they divided Longxi into Jincheng, Xiping, and other commanderies, mixed with Di and Qiang dwelling there.
translations.idiomatic: Longxi was split into Jincheng, Xiping, and other prefectures where Di and Qiang peoples were settled among the Han.

sentences.zh: 歷代喪亂，不為賢豪所據，則為遠夷侵廢；

translations.literal: Through successive dynasties, in times of ruin and turmoil, if not held by worthy and powerful men, then it was invaded and abandoned by distant barbarians;
translations.idiomatic: Dynasty after dynasty, whenever no strong lord held it, distant peoples invaded and laid it waste;

sentences.zh: 迨千年矣。

translations.literal: This has extended nearly a thousand years.
translations.idiomatic: A thousand years have passed in that cycle.

sentences.zh: 武德初。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wude.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Wude era.

sentences.zh: 薛仁杲奄有隴上之地，至於河虜。

translations.literal: Xue Rengao suddenly held the lands atop Long, reaching to the river barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Rengao seized the Long plateau and pressed to the river frontier.

sentences.zh: 李敷盡有涼州之域，通於磧外。

translations.literal: Li Fu wholly possessed the territory of Liang Prefecture, reaching through to beyond the desert.
translations.idiomatic: Li Fu held all Liangzhou and his sway ran past the desert's edge.

sentences.zh: 貞觀中，李靖破吐谷渾，侯君集平高昌，阿史那社爾開西域，置四鎮。

translations.literal: In Zhenguan, Li Jing defeated Tuyuhun; Hou Junji pacified Gaochang; Ashina She'er opened the Western Regions and established the Four Garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhenguan, Li Jing shattered Tuyuhun, Hou Junji subdued Gaochang, and Ashina She'er opened the west and planted the Four Garrisons.

sentences.zh: 前王之所未伏，盡為臣妾，秦、漢之封域，得議其土境耶！

translations.literal: What former kings had not subjugated was all made servant and concubine; could one negotiate the soil boundaries of Qin and Han's enfeoffed domains!
translations.idiomatic: Kingdoms no earlier throne had broken all bowed as subjects—could one still haggle over the old domains of Qin and Han!

sentences.zh: 於是歲調山東丁男為戍卒，繒帛為軍資，有屯田以資糗糧，牧使以娩羊馬。

translations.literal: Thereupon each year men of Shandong were levied as garrison soldiers, silk and brocade as military funds; there was frontier farming to supply grain provisions; herd commissioners to breed sheep and horses.
translations.idiomatic: Each year levies drew men from east of the mountains to man the walls, silk to fill the war chests; colony fields fed the garrisons and herd offices bred sheep and horses.

sentences.zh: 大軍萬人，小軍千人，烽戍邏卒，萬里相繼，以卻於強敵。

translations.literal: Great armies ten thousand men, small armies a thousand men, beacon garrisons and frontier patrol soldiers, ten thousand li in succession, thereby to repel the strong enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Hosts of ten thousand and detachments of a thousand, beacon towers and frontier patrols linked for ten thousand li, held the line against powerful foes.

sentences.zh: 隴右鄯州為節度。

translations.literal: Longyou with Shan Prefecture was made a military commission.
translations.idiomatic: Longyou was centered on Shan as a frontier command.

sentences.zh: 河西涼州為節度。

translations.literal: Hexi with Liang Prefecture was made a military commission.
translations.idiomatic: Hexi was centered on Liang as a military command.

sentences.zh: 安西、北庭亦置節度，關內則於靈州置朔方節度，又有受降城、單於都護庭為之籓衛。

translations.literal: Anxi and Beiting also had military commissions established; within the passes, at Ling Prefecture Shuofang commission was placed; moreover there were Shouxiang City and the Chanyu Protectorate court as its outer defense.
translations.idiomatic: Anxi and Beiting received commissioners as well; within the passes Shuofang was established at Lingzhou, with Shouxiang City and the Chanyu Protectorate as its shield.

sentences.zh: 及潼關失守，河洛阻兵，於是盡征河隴、朔方之將鎮兵入靖國難，謂之行營。

translations.literal: When Tong Pass was lost and He-Luo blocked by war, thereupon all generals and garrison troops of He-Long and Shuofang were levied to enter and pacify the national calamity—called the mobile camp.
translations.idiomatic: When Tong Pass fell and the heartland drowned in war, every frontier general and garrison of He-Long and Shuofang was summoned east to save the dynasty—these were called the campaigning hosts.

sentences.zh: 曩時軍營邊州無備預矣。

translations.literal: The military camps and border prefectures of former times had no preparations left.
translations.idiomatic: The border strongholds were stripped bare of defense.

sentences.zh: 乾元之後，吐蕃乘我間隙，日蹙邊城，或為虜掠傷殺，或轉死溝壑。

translations.literal: After Qianyuan, Tubo seized our gaps; day by day they pressed upon border cities—some were looted and wounded or killed by the foe; some died turning in ditches and gullies.
translations.idiomatic: After the Qianyuan era Tubo exploited our weakness, tightening day by day on the frontier forts—some fell to slaughter and plunder, others to starvation in the gullies.

sentences.zh: 數年之後，鳳翔之西，邠州之北，盡蕃戎之境，淹沒者數十州。

translations.literal: After several years, west of Fengxiang, north of Bin—altogether Tubo and barbarian territory; drowned and lost were dozens of prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few years everything west of Fengxiang and north of Bin became barbarian ground; dozens of prefectures were swallowed.

sentences.zh: 肅宗元年建寅月甲辰，吐蕃遣使來朝請和，敕宰相郭子儀、蕭華、裴遵慶等於中書設宴。

translations.literal: On jiachen day of the jiayin month of the first year of Suzong, Tubo sent envoys to court seeking peace; an edict ordered Chancellors Guo Ziyi, Xiao Hua, Pei Zunqing, and others to set a banquet at the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: On the first jiayin month's jiachen day of Suzong's first year Tubo envoys came suing for peace; Guo Ziyi, Xiao Hua, Pei Zunqing, and other chancellors were ordered to host them at the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 將詣光宇寺為盟誓，使者云：蕃法盟誓，取三牲血歃之，無向佛寺之事，請明日須於鴻臚寺歃血，以申蕃戎之禮。

translations.literal: They were about to go to Guangyu Temple to make the covenant oath; the envoys said: By Tubo law covenant oaths take the blood of the three sacrificial animals and drink it in oath; there is no matter of going to Buddhist temples; we request that tomorrow blood-oath must be at the Court of State Ceremonial, to declare Tubo barbarian ritual.
translations.idiomatic: When the court prepared to swear the pact at Guangyu Temple, the envoys said: "By Tubo custom we mix the blood of three beasts and drink the oath—we do not swear in temples. Let us meet tomorrow at the Court of State Ceremonial and perform the blood rite as Tubo law requires."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: [The court] followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 寶應元年六月，吐蕃使燭番、莽耳等二人貢方物入朝，乃於延英殿引見，勞賜各有差。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the first year of Baoying, Tubo envoys Zhu Fan, Mang Er, and two others presented tribute goods at court; they were then received in audience at Yanying Hall; rewards and gifts differed by rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Baoying 1, Tubo envoys Zhu Fan and Mang Er brought tribute to court and were received in Yanying Hall, each rewarded according to his station.

sentences.zh: 而劍南西山又與吐蕃、氐、羌鄰接，武德以來，開置州縣，立軍防，即漢之笮路，乾元之後，亦陷於吐蕃。

translations.literal: Moreover the western mountains of Jiannan again bordered Tubo, Di, and Qiang; from Wude onward, prefectures and counties were opened and established, military defenses set up—this was Han's Zuo Road; after Qianyuan, it too fell to Tubo.
translations.idiomatic: The western ranges of Jiannan likewise marched with Tubo, Di, and Qiang. Since Wude the court had opened prefectures and garrison posts along the old Han Zuo Road; after Qianyuan that country too was lost to Tubo.

sentences.zh: 寶慶二年三月，遣左散騎常侍兼御史大夫李之芳、左庶子兼御史中丞崔倫使於吐蕃，至其境而留之。

translations.literal: In the third month of the second year of Baoxing, Left Regular Attendant and Concurrent Censor-in-Chief Li Zhifang and Left Household Companion and Concurrent Vice Censor-in-Chief Cui Lun were sent as envoys to Tubo; reaching its borders they were detained.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Baoying 2 the court sent Li Zhifang and Cui Lun as envoys to Tubo; once they reached the frontier the Tibetans held them.

sentences.zh: 廣德元年九月，吐蕃寇陷涇州。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the first year of Guangde, Tubo raided and captured Jing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of Guangde 1 Tubo stormed and took Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 十月，寇邠州，又陷奉天縣。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, they raided Bin Prefecture and also captured Fengtian County.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month they struck Binzhou and seized Fengtian County.

sentences.zh: 遣中書令郭子儀西禦。

translations.literal: Chief Minister Guo Ziyi was sent west to resist them.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Guo Ziyi was dispatched west to meet them.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃以吐谷渾、党項羌之眾二十余萬，自龍光度而東。

translations.literal: Tubo with Tuyuhun and Tangut Qiang masses of more than two hundred thousand, from Longguang Ford marched east.
translations.idiomatic: Tubo led more than two hundred thousand Tuyuhun and Tangut Qiang warriors east from Longguang Ford.

sentences.zh: 郭子儀退軍，車駕幸陜州，京師失守。

translations.literal: Guo Ziyi withdrew his army; the imperial carriage went in favor to Shan Prefecture; the capital was lost and not held.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi fell back; the emperor fled to Shanzhou; the capital fell.

sentences.zh: 降將高暉引吐蕃入上都城，與吐蕃大將馬重英等立故邠王男廣武王承宏為帝，立年號，大赦，署置官員，尋以司封崔瑰等為相。

translations.literal: The surrendered general Gao Hui led Tubo into the Upper Capital city; with Tubo great general Ma Chongying and others they installed Li Chenghong, Prince of Guangwu, as emperor, established an era name, proclaimed a general amnesty, appointed and set officials; soon they made Director of Enfeoffments Cui Gui and others chancellors.
translations.idiomatic: The defector Gao Hui guided Tubo into the Upper Capital; with the Tubo commander Ma Chongying and others they enthroned Li Chenghong, Prince of Guangwu, proclaimed a reign title and general amnesty, and soon named Cui Gui of the Directorate of Enfeoffments and others as chancellors.

sentences.zh: 郭子儀退軍南保商州，吐蕃居城十五日退，官軍收上都，以郭子儀為留守。

translations.literal: Guo Ziyi withdrew his army south to hold Shang Prefecture; Tubo occupied the city fifteen days then withdrew; the government army recovered the Upper Capital; Guo Ziyi was made garrison commander.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi fell back south to Shangzhou; the Tibetans held the capital fifteen days and withdrew; the imperial army retook the Upper Capital and made Guo Ziyi its garrison commander.

sentences.zh: 初，車駕東幸，衣冠戚裏盡南投荊襄及隱竄山谷，於是六軍將士持兵剽劫，所在阻絕。

translations.literal: At first, when the imperial carriage went east in favor, officials and gentry and imperial kin all fled south to Jing-Xiang and hid in seclusion in mountain valleys; thereupon the Six Armies officers and soldiers took weapons and plundered; everywhere was blocked and cut off.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor fled east, courtiers and kin scattered south to Jingxiang or hid in the hills; the Six Armies then turned to armed robbery, and travel was cut off everywhere.

sentences.zh: 郭子儀領部曲數百人及其妻子仆從南入牛心谷，駝馬車牛數百兩，子儀遲留，未知所適。

translations.literal: Guo Ziyi led several hundred retainers of his command together with their wives, children, and servants south into Niuxin Valley, with several hundred teams of camels, horses, carts, and oxen; Ziyi lingered, not knowing where to go.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi led several hundred retainers with their families south into Niuxin Valley, driving hundreds of pack animals and carts, and lingered there uncertain which way to turn.

sentences.zh: 行軍判官、中書舍人王延昌、監察御史李萼謂子儀曰：「令公身為元帥，主上蒙塵於外，家國之事，一至於此。

translations.literal: Campaigning army judge Wang Yanchang, Secretariat Drafter, and Investigative Censor Li E said to Ziyi: "Lord, you are marshal in person; the sovereign is dust-stained abroad; affairs of family and state have come to this.
translations.idiomatic: The army judge Wang Yanchang, a Secretariat drafter, and the censor Li E said to him: "You are the supreme commander, yet the emperor wanders in exile—never has the realm come to such a pass.

sentences.zh: 今吐蕃之勢日逼，豈可懷安於谷中，何不南趨商州，漸赴行在。

translations.literal: Now Tubo's momentum presses day by day; how can you cherish ease in the valley? Why not hurry south toward Shang Prefecture and gradually reach the mobile court?
translations.idiomatic: Tubo presses closer every day—how can you rest easy in this gorge? March south to Shangzhou and rejoin the emperor's court.

sentences.zh: 」子儀遽從之。

translations.literal: Ziyi hastily followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi at once agreed.

sentences.zh: 延昌曰：「吐蕃知令公南行，必分兵來逼，若當大路，事即危矣。

translations.literal: Yanchang said: "If Tubo knows the Lord is marching south, they will surely divide troops to press; if you take the main road, the matter will at once be perilous.
translations.idiomatic: Yanchang said: "Once Tubo learns you are heading south they will send detachments after you—take the highway and you are lost.

sentences.zh: 不如取玉山路而去，出其不意。

translations.literal: Better to take the Yushan road and go, striking where they do not expect.
translations.idiomatic: Better strike out on the Yushan trail and take them unawares.

sentences.zh: 」子儀又從之。

translations.literal: Ziyi again followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi agreed again.

sentences.zh: 延昌與李萼皆從子儀，子儀之隊千余人，山路狹隘，連延百餘里，人不得馳。

translations.literal: Yanchang and Li E both followed Ziyi; Ziyi's column was more than a thousand men; the mountain road was narrow and confined, extending more than a hundred li, and men could not gallop.
translations.idiomatic: Yanchang and Li E rode with him—over a thousand in Guo Ziyi's column on a narrow track more than a hundred li long where no one could ride at speed.

sentences.zh: 延昌與萼恐狹徑被追，前後不相救，至倒回口，遂與子儀別行，逾絕澗，登七盤，趨於商州。

translations.literal: Yanchang and E feared that on the narrow path if pursued, front and rear could not rescue one another; reaching Daohuikou, they then traveled separately from Ziyi, crossed sheer ravines, ascended Seven Bends, and hastened toward Shang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing pursuit on the defile where front and rear could not aid each other, they parted from Guo Ziyi at Daohuikou, crossed the cliffs by Seven Bends, and made for Shangzhou.

sentences.zh: 先是，六軍將張知節與麾下數百人自京城奔於商州，大掠避難朝官、士庶及居人資財鞍馬，已有日矣。

translations.literal: Earlier, Six Armies general Zhang Zhijie with several hundred under his command had fled from the capital to Shang Prefecture and greatly plundered fleeing court officials, commoners, and residents' goods, wealth, saddles, and horses—for days already.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Zhang Zhijie of the Six Armies had fled the capital to Shangzhou with several hundred men and for days had been plundering refugees, townspeople, and their goods and mounts.

sentences.zh: 延昌與萼既至，說知節曰：「將軍身掌禁兵，軍敗而不赴行在，又恣其下虜掠，何所歸乎？

translations.literal: Yanchang and E having arrived, persuaded Zhijie saying: "General, you hold the forbidden army; the army was defeated yet you did not go to the mobile court, and again let your subordinates loot captives—where will you return?
translations.idiomatic: When they arrived they urged Zhang Zhijie: "You command the imperial guard, yet after defeat you neither rejoined the court nor restrained your men from looting—where can that end?

sentences.zh: 今郭令公元帥也，已欲至洛南，將軍若整頓士卒，喻以禍福，請令公來撫之，以圖收長安，此則將軍非常之功也。

translations.literal: Now Lord Guo is marshal; he already intends to reach Luonan; if the General rallies the soldiers and explains fortune and calamity, and asks the Lord to come and reassure them, to plan recovering Chang'an—this then is the General's extraordinary achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Marshal Guo is near Luonan. Rally your troops, show them what honor or ruin awaits, and ask him to lead you—all to win back Chang'an. That would be a feat beyond measure.

sentences.zh: 」知節大悅。

translations.literal: Zhijie was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhijie was delighted.

sentences.zh: 其時諸軍將臧希讓、高升、彭體盈、李惟詵等數人，各有部曲，率其數十騎，相次而至，又從其計，皆相率為軍，約不侵暴。

translations.literal: At that time various army generals Zang Xirang, Gao Sheng, Peng Tiying, Li Weishen, and several others, each with their own commands, led their several tens of horsemen, arriving one after another; they again followed this plan; all together led one another as an army, agreeing not to invade or commit violence.
translations.idiomatic: Then other generals—Zang Xirang, Gao Sheng, Peng Tiying, Li Weishen, and others—arrived in turn with their bands, accepted the plan, and formed a united force pledged not to plunder.

sentences.zh: 延昌留於軍中主約，萼以數騎往迎子儀，去洛南十餘里，及之，遂與子儀回至商州。

translations.literal: Yanchang remained in the army to preside over the covenant; E with several horsemen went to welcome Ziyi; more than ten li from Luonan they reached him, and thereupon returned with Ziyi to Shang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yanchang stayed with the troops to hold them to the pact while Li E rode out with a few men to meet Guo Ziyi, found him a dozen li south of Luonan, and brought him back to Shangzhou.

sentences.zh: 諸將大喜，皆遵其約束。

translations.literal: The generals were all greatly pleased and all obeyed the restraints.
translations.idiomatic: The generals rejoiced and kept the discipline he had imposed.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃將入京師也，前光祿卿殷仲卿逃難而出，鞍馬衣服盡為土賊所掠。

translations.literal: When Tubo was about to enter the capital, former Chamberlain for Ceremonials Yin Zhongqing fled in hardship; saddle, horse, and clothing were all plundered by local bandits.
translations.idiomatic: As Tubo prepared to enter the capital, the former Chamberlain Yin Zhongqing fled; bandits stripped him of horse, saddle, and robes.

sentences.zh: 仲卿至藍田，糾合散兵及諸驍勇願從者百余人，南保藍田，以拒吐蕃，其眾漸振，至於千人。

translations.literal: Zhongqing reached Lantian, gathered scattered soldiers and all brave men willing to follow—more than a hundred men—held Lantian southward to resist Tubo; his masses gradually revived, reaching a thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: At Lantian he gathered a hundred-odd stragglers and volunteers, held the district against Tubo, and his force grew to a thousand.

sentences.zh: 子儀既至商州，未知仲卿之舉，募人往探賊勢。

translations.literal: Ziyi having reached Shang Prefecture, did not yet know Zhongqing's action; he recruited men to go probe the rebels' momentum.
translations.idiomatic: Once Guo Ziyi reached Shangzhou he did not yet know of Yin Zhongqing's stand and sent men to scout the enemy.

sentences.zh: 羽林將軍長孫全緒請行，以二百騎隸之。

translations.literal: Palace Guard General Zhangsun Quanxu requested to go; two hundred cavalry were attached to him.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Guard General Zhangsun Quanxu volunteered and was given two hundred horsemen.

sentences.zh: 又令太子賓客第五琦攝京兆尹，同收長安。

translations.literal: He also ordered the Crown Prince's guest Diwu Qi to act as provisional metropolitan governor of Jingzhao, to recover Chang'an together.
translations.idiomatic: He also appointed the Crown Prince's adviser Diwu Qi acting metropolitan governor of Jingzhao to join in retaking Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 全緒至韓公堆，晝則擊鼓，廣張旗幟，夜則多燃火，以疑吐蕃。

translations.literal: Quanxu reached Hanggongdui; by day he beat drums and spread banners widely; by night he lit many fires, to make Tubo doubtful.
translations.idiomatic: At Hanggongdui, Zhangsun Quanxu beat drums by day, flew banners in profusion, and lit many fires by night to deceive the Tubo army.

sentences.zh: 仲卿探知官軍，其勢益壯。

translations.literal: Zhongqing probed and learned of the government army; his momentum grew stronger.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Zhongqing learned that imperial troops were near, and his force grew bolder.

sentences.zh: 遂相為表裏，以狀聞於子儀。

translations.literal: Thereupon they acted as inner and outer wings, and reported the situation to Ziyi.
translations.idiomatic: The two columns then coordinated as inner and outer wings and sent word of their position to Guo Ziyi.

sentences.zh: 仲卿帥二百余騎遊奕，直渡浐水。

translations.literal: Zhongqing led more than two hundred horsemen on patrol, crossing the Chan River straight across.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Zhongqing led more than two hundred horsemen on patrol and crossed the Chan River at a ford.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃懼，問百姓，百姓皆紿之曰：「郭令公自商州領眾卻收長安，大軍不知其數。

translations.literal: Tubo was afraid; questioning the common people, the common people all deceived them saying: "Lord Guo from Shang Prefecture leads the masses to turn back and recover Chang'an; the great army's number is unknown."
translations.idiomatic: The Tubo troops grew fearful and questioned local people, who all lied to them: "Marshal Guo is marching from Shangzhou with a host to retake Chang'an—no one knows how great that army is."

sentences.zh: 」賊以為然，遂抽軍而還，余眾尚在城。

translations.literal: " The rebels believed it true, and thereupon drew off the army and returned; the remaining masses were still in the city.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy believed them, drew off the main body, and left only a remnant in the city.

sentences.zh: 軍將王撫及御史大夫王仲升頓兵自苑中入，椎鼓大呼，仲卿之師又入城，吐蕃皆奔走，乃收上都。

translations.literal: Army commander Wang Fu and censor-in-chief Wang Zhongsheng halted troops entering from within the park, beat drums and shouted loudly; Zhongqing's army again entered the city; Tubo all fled in panic; thereupon they recovered the upper capital.
translations.idiomatic: The commanders Wang Fu and Censor-in-Chief Wang Zhongsheng led troops in from the imperial park, beating drums and shouting; Yin Zhongqing's men entered the walls as well. The Tubo soldiers broke and ran, and the upper capital was retaken.

sentences.zh: 郭子儀乘之，鼓行入長安，人心乃安。

translations.literal: Guo Ziyi seized the moment; beating drums he marched into Chang'an; the people's hearts were then at peace.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi pressed the advantage, entered Chang'an to the beat of drums, and the people's hearts were steadied.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃退至鳳翔，節度孫誌直閉門拒之，吐蕃圍守數日。

translations.literal: Tubo retreated to Fengxiang; military commissioner Sun Zhizhi closed the gates to reject them; Tubo besieged and held for several days.
translations.idiomatic: Tubo fell back on Fengxiang, but the military commissioner Sun Zhizhi shut the gates against them; the Tubo army besieged the city for days.

sentences.zh: 會鎮西節度、兼御史中丞馬璘領精騎千余自河西救楊誌烈回，引兵入城。

translations.literal: It happened that frontier military commissioner and concurrent vice censor-in-chief Ma Lin led more than a thousand elite horsemen from Hexi to rescue Yang Zhilie and return, and led troops into the city.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Lin, military commissioner of the western frontier and concurrent vice censor-in-chief, came from Hexi with more than a thousand picked horsemen, rescued Yang Zhilie on his return, and led his men into Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 遲明，單騎持滿，直沖賊眾，左右願從者百余騎。

translations.literal: At dawn he rode alone with bow fully drawn, charging straight into the rebel masses; left and right, more than a hundred horsemen wished to follow.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn he rode out alone, bow drawn full, and charged the enemy ranks; a little over a hundred horsemen who wished to follow went with him.

sentences.zh: 璘奮擊大呼，賊徒披靡，無敢當者，賊疲而歸。

translations.literal: Lin struck fiercely with great shouts; the rebel band scattered; none dared withstand; the rebels, weary, returned.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Lin charged shouting; the enemy lines split and none dared stand before him. The raiders, exhausted, withdrew.

sentences.zh: 賊眾恃其驍勇，翌日又逼城請戰。

translations.literal: The rebel masses relied on their fierce bravery; the next day again pressed the city and requested battle.
translations.idiomatic: Trusting in their fierceness, the enemy came back the next day and pressed the walls, demanding battle.

sentences.zh: 璘披甲開懸門，賊乃抽退。

translations.literal: Lin donned armor and opened the drawbridge; the rebels then drew off and retreated.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Lin armored himself and opened the drawbridge; the enemy at once pulled back.

sentences.zh: 皆曰：「此將不惜死不可當，且避之。

translations.literal: All said: "This general, who does not spare his life, cannot be withstood; let us for the present avoid him."
translations.idiomatic: They said among themselves, "This commander cares nothing for his life—we cannot face him. Better withdraw for now."

sentences.zh: 」又復居原、會、成、渭之地。

translations.literal: " Again they occupied the lands of Yuan, Hui, Cheng, and Wei.
translations.idiomatic: They then reoccupied the prefectures of Yuan, Hui, Cheng, and Wei.

sentences.zh: 十二月，乘輿還上都。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month the imperial carriage returned to the upper capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month the emperor returned to the upper capital.

sentences.zh: 二年五月，放李之芳還。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the second year Li Zhifang was released to return.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the second year Li Zhifang was sent home from captivity.

sentences.zh: 九月，叛將僕射、大寧郡王仆固懷恩自靈武遣其黨範誌誠、任敷等引吐蕃、吐谷渾之眾來犯王畿。

translations.literal: In the ninth month the rebel general, Pushe, Prince of Daning commandery Pugu Huai'en from Lingwu sent his partisans Fan Zhicheng, Ren Fu, and others to lead Tubo and Tuyuhun masses to invade the royal domain.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month the rebel Pugu Huai'en, Prince of Daning and former Pushe, sent his followers Fan Zhicheng and Ren Fu from Lingwu to bring Tubo and Tuyuhun forces against the capital region.

sentences.zh: 十月，懷恩之眾至邠州挑戰，節度白孝德及副元帥先鋒郭鋒嬰城拒之，以挫其鋒。

translations.literal: In the tenth month Huai'en's masses reached Bin Prefecture and challenged battle; military commissioner Bai Xiaode and the deputy grand marshal's vanguard Guo Feng held the city to reject them, to blunt their edge.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Huai'en's army reached Binzhou and offered battle. The military commissioner Bai Xiaode and the vanguard of the deputy grand marshal, Guo Feng, shut the walls and held firm to blunt the enemy's momentum.

sentences.zh: 賊眾遂逼奉天縣西二十里為營，郭子儀屯於奉天，又按軍不戰。

translations.literal: The rebel masses thereupon pressed Fengtian county twenty li west and made camp; Guo Ziyi encamped at Fengtian, again restraining the army and not fighting.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels then pitched camp twenty li west of Fengtian county while Guo Ziyi held Fengtian and again kept his army in check without giving battle.

sentences.zh: 郭鋒於邠州西三十里，令精騎二百五十人、步卒五十人斫懷恩營，破五千眾，斬首千余級，生擒八十五人，降其大將四人，為五百匹。

translations.literal: Guo Feng thirty li west of Bin Prefecture ordered two hundred fifty elite horsemen and fifty foot soldiers to strike Huai'en's camp, broke five thousand masses, beheaded more than a thousand heads, captured alive eighty-five men, caused four of their great generals to surrender, and took five hundred horses.
translations.idiomatic: Thirty li west of Binzhou, Guo Feng sent two hundred fifty picked horsemen and fifty foot soldiers to raid Huai'en's camp. They routed five thousand men, took more than a thousand heads, captured eighty-five alive, received the surrender of four enemy generals, and seized five hundred horses.

sentences.zh: 十一月，仆固懷恩引吐蕃之眾退。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month Pugu Huai'en led Tubo masses to withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Pugu Huai'en withdrew with the Tubo forces.

sentences.zh: 廣德二年，河西節度楊誌烈被圍，守數年，以孤城無援，乃跳身西投甘州，涼州又陷於寇。

translations.literal: In the second year of Guangde, Hexi military commissioner Yang Zhilie was besieged; he held for several years; because the lone city had no relief, he then leapt away west and fled to Gan Prefecture; Liang Prefecture again fell to the invaders.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Guangde the Hexi commissioner Yang Zhilie, besieged for years in an isolated city without relief, slipped away west to Ganzhou; Liangzhou then fell to the enemy.

sentences.zh: 永泰元年三月，吐蕃請和，遣宰相元載、杜鴻漸等於興唐寺與之盟而罷。

translations.literal: In the third month of the first year of Yongtai Tubo requested peace; the court sent chancellors Yuan Zai, Du Hongjian, and others to ally with them at Xingtang Temple and then cease.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Yongtai 1 Tubo sued for peace, and chancellors Yuan Zai and Du Hongjian met their envoys at Xingtang Temple to swear an alliance.

sentences.zh: 秋九月，仆固懷恩誘吐蕃、回紇之眾，南犯王畿。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of autumn Pugu Huai'en enticed Tubo and Uyghur masses to invade the royal domain southward.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn, in the ninth month, Pugu Huai'en incited Tubo and Uyghur forces to march south against the capital region.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃大將尚結息贊磨、尚息東贊、尚野息及馬重英率二十萬眾至奉天界，邠州節度使白孝德不能禦，京城戒嚴。

translations.literal: Tubo great generals Shang Jiexi Zanmo, Shang Xidongzan, Shang Yexi, and Ma Chongying led two hundred thousand masses to the border of Fengtian; Bin Prefecture military commissioner Bai Xiaode could not withstand them; the capital was placed under strict guard.
translations.idiomatic: The Tubo generals Shang Jiexi Zanmo, Shang Xidongzan, Shang Yexi, and Ma Chongying advanced with two hundred thousand men to Fengtian. The Binzhou commissioner Bai Xiaode could not hold them, and the capital went on full alert.

sentences.zh: 先是，朔方先鋒兵馬使渾日進、孫守亮屯軍於奉天以拒之，於是詔追副元帥郭子儀於河中府領眾赴援，屯於涇陽，諸將各屯守要害。

translations.literal: Earlier, Shuofang vanguard army-and-horse commissioner Hun Rijin and Sun Shouliang encamped at Fengtian to resist them; thereupon an edict recalled deputy grand marshal Guo Ziyi at Hezhong prefecture to lead masses to rush to aid, encamped at Jingyang, and the various generals each encamped and guarded strategic points.
translations.idiomatic: Hun Rijin and Sun Shouliang of the Shuofang vanguard were already holding Fengtian. The court then recalled Deputy Grand Marshal Guo Ziyi from Hezhong with his army, posted him at Jingyang, and stationed other generals at key points.

sentences.zh: 初，吐蕃列營奉天，渾日進單騎沖之，驍騎二百人繼進，沖突其營，左右擊刺，賊徒驚駭，無不應弦而斃。

translations.literal: At first Tubo arrayed camps at Fengtian; Hun Rijin alone on horseback charged them; two hundred fierce horsemen followed in advance; they burst into the camps, striking left and right; the rebel band was alarmed and terrified; none failed to fall dead at the bowstring.
translations.idiomatic: When Tubo first encamped at Fengtian, Hun Rijin charged their lines alone, two hundred crack horsemen close behind. They tore through the camp striking left and right until every arrow found its mark and the enemy broke in panic.

sentences.zh: 日進挾一蕃將，躍馬而歸，蕃將奮身，失其撒飯一。

translations.literal: Rijin seized one Tubo general, leaped on horse and returned; the Tubo general struggled with his body; he lost one sash-plaque (sapan).
translations.idiomatic: Hun Rijin seized a Tubo officer and galloped back with him; the man wrenched free but lost a belt plaque in the struggle.

sentences.zh: 日進之眾，無中鋒鏑者，軍中望而益振。

translations.literal: Of Rijin's masses none were struck by arrowheads; the army gazing upon this was the more inspired.
translations.idiomatic: Not one of Hun Rijin's men took an arrow wound, and the army took fresh heart at the sight.

sentences.zh: 明日，吐蕃悉眾圍之，日進命拋車夾石投之，雜以弓弩，賊死傷眾。

translations.literal: The next day Tubo mustered all masses and besieged them; Rijin ordered catapults to hurl stones, mixed with bows and crossbows; the rebels died and were wounded in great numbers.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Tubo surrounded them in full force. Hun Rijin ordered catapults to shower stones, mixed with bow and crossbow fire, and the enemy fell in great numbers.

sentences.zh: 數日，斂軍回營。

translations.literal: After several days they gathered the army and returned to camp.
translations.idiomatic: After several days he drew his troops back into camp.

sentences.zh: 尋又日進夜斫賊營於梁母神下，殺千余人，生擒五百人，獲駝馬器械。

translations.literal: Soon again Rijin by night struck the rebel camp below Liangmu Shrine, killed more than a thousand men, captured alive five hundred men, and obtained camels, horses, and weapons.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Hun Rijin raided the enemy camp by night below Liangmu Shrine, killed more than a thousand, took five hundred alive, and seized camels, horses, and arms.

sentences.zh: 上又下詔親征，括朝官馬，京城置團練。

translations.literal: The emperor again issued an edict for a personal campaign, requisitioned court officials' horses, and established militia training in the capital.
